topic: Lead Bank Scheme and Service Area Approach
t: Lead Bank Scheme → origin and basic aim
text:
Item | Fact
Idea | Gadgil Study Group (Oct 1969): Area Approach
Endorsed | Nariman Committee (bankers, Nov 1969): each bank to act as Lead Bank for certain districts
Launched | December 1969 by RBI
Unit | District
Lead bank | A bank designated for the district (not necessarily SBI)
Last reviewed | Usha Thorat High Level Committee, 2009
Aim: individual banks adopt particular districts for intensive development
Lead bank coordinates all credit institutions and government agencies to raise credit to priority sector and rural development
District credit planning is done under the Lead Bank (UPPCS 2002-03)
⚠ Not "big banks open offices in each district", not "competition among banks", not "deposit mobilisation"
PYQ 2012: basic aim = banks adopt districts for intensive development

t: SHG-Bank Linkage Programme → who started it, who implements it
text:
Item | Fact
Started by | NABARD, 1992 (1992-93)
Aim | Link SHGs of the poor with the formal banking system
Implemented by | Commercial banks, RRBs, cooperative banks
Not implemented by | NABARD itself (it refinances)
Loan basis | Group guarantee, no collateral

t: SHG → features and functioning (NCERT)
text:
Feature | Fact
Size | 15-20 members, one neighbourhood, mostly women
Saving | Rs 25 to Rs 100 or more per member, regularly
Internal loans | From pooled savings; interest lower than moneylenders
Bank loan | After 1-2 years of regular saving; sanctioned in the name of the group
Liability | Group responsible for repayment; non-repayment followed up by members
Decisions | Taken by members (purpose, amount, interest, repayment)
Overcomes lack of collateral; also a platform for health, nutrition, domestic violence issues
Evolution (Testbook): TLA women's wing, Ahmedabad, 1954; MYRADA (Karnataka) groups in the 1980s
⚠ "In an SHG all members take responsibility for one member's loan" - correct (2023 statement 2)

t: Microfinance → meaning and the four services

Service | Example
Credit | Small collateral-free loans
Savings | Savings accounts, thrift

PMSBY | Accident cover (annual renewable) | 18-70 | ₹20 a year

## Beyond your notes
PMSBY pays ₹2 lakh for death/full disability, ₹1 lakh for partial disability

topic: NPCI, RuPay and the payment architecture
t: NPCI → status, promoters and functions
text:
## 1. What NPCI is
Attribute | Fact
Set up | 2008, Mumbai
Promoted by | RBI and Indian Banks' Association (IBA)
Legal form | Not-for-profit company under Section 8, Companies Act 2013
Legal basis for its role | Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
Role | Umbrella entity for retail payments and settlement in India
Supervised by | RBI
Bank-led: public sector banks hold the majority stake (PMF LENS May 2025)
Core promoter banks (Testbook): SBI, PNB, Canara, BoB, Union Bank, Bank of India, ICICI, HDFC, Citibank, HSBC
⚠ NPCI is not a statutory body and not a government department; it is a Section 8 company
⚠ NPCI runs retail systems; RTGS and NEFT are run by RBI, not NPCI
PYQ 2017: NPCI promotes financial inclusion and launched RuPay → both correct

topic: NPCI, RuPay and the payment architecture
t: NPCI → which system links all ATMs (NFS)
text:
National Financial Switch (NFS) = largest network of shared ATMs in India; lets a customer use any bank's ATM
Step | Fact
Built by | RBI's IDRBT (Institute for Development and Research in Banking Technology)
Year deployed | 2004
Taken over by NPCI | December 2009
Function | Interconnects all ATMs in the country
⚠ Not linked by IBA, NSDL or RBI directly: the answer is NPCI
PYQ 2018: "Which one links all the ATMs in India?" → National Payments Corporation of India; trap: IBA is a promoter, not the operator
## 2. NPCI's international arm
NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL): subsidiary that takes UPI and RuPay abroad

topic: NPCI, RuPay and the payment architecture
t: NPCI products → what each system does
text:
System | Function
UPI | Real-time, interoperable bank-to-bank mobile payments
IMPS | Instant 24x7 interbank transfer (base on which UPI was built)
RuPay | Indigenous card network (debit, credit, prepaid)
BHIM | NPCI's own UPI app
NFS | Shared ATM network
NACH | Bulk, repetitive payments: salaries, subsidies, pensions, dividends, EMIs
AePS | Aadhaar Enabled Payment System: banking via Aadhaar + biometrics through business correspondents
BBPS | Bharat Bill Payment System: recurring bills
NETC FASTag | Electronic toll collection
Bharat QR | Interoperable QR for merchant payments (with Visa and Mastercard)
UPI 123PAY | UPI for feature phones without internet
⚠ NEFT, RTGS = RBI; IMPS, UPI, NACH, BBPS, AePS = NPCI (PMF LENS Oct 2025)
## 3. Single-point risk
NPCI routes nearly all UPI transactions (encrypts PIN, forwards to banks): any NPCI downtime halts UPI
2025 UPI outages blamed on banks flooding NPCI with status-check requests (PMF LENS May 2025)

topic: NPCI, RuPay and the payment architecture
t: RuPay → features and objectives
text:
## 1. Basics
Indigenous card network launched by NPCI in 2012 (Preview)
Variants: debit, credit, prepaid, Kisan, contactless (NFC)
Feature | Fact
Network fee | Issuing banks pay no network registration fee (unlike Visa/Mastercard)
MDR | Lower than international networks; zero MDR on RuPay debit since 2020
Data | Processed and stored largely within India
Jan Dhan | Free RuPay debit card with ₹2 lakh accident cover (accounts after 28.8.2018)
Credit on UPI | RuPay credit cards can be linked to UPI
## 2. Objectives (PMF S&T)
Cut dependence on foreign card networks; financial inclusion; lower costs; payment sovereignty
⚠ Zero MDR covers RuPay debit cards, not RuPay credit cards
RuPay accepted abroad in select countries: Singapore, Bhutan, UAE, Bahrain, Saudi Arabia (Testbook); RuPay launched in Mauritius (PMF)

topic: NPCI, RuPay and the payment architecture
t: Payment regulation → PSS Act, PRB and New Umbrella Entities
text:
## 1. Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
Gives RBI power to regulate and supervise payment systems
Section 10A (added 2019): no charges (MDR) on notified electronic modes
## 2. Payments Regulatory Board (PRB)
Feature | Fact
Members | Six
Chair | RBI Governor
Others | Deputy Governor, an RBI Executive Director, 3 Centre nominees
Replaced | BPSS (5-member RBI board, no government members)
Powers from | PSS Act, 2007
Meets | At least twice a year; quorum 3; chair has casting vote
⚠ PRB has government nominees; the old BPSS had none
## 3. New Umbrella Entity (NUE) for retail payments (Testbook)
Aim: competition to NPCI's monopoly in retail payments
Min paid-up capital ₹500 crore; no promoter group above 40%; owned and controlled by residents; 3 years' payment experience

topic: UPI, BHIM, wallets and UPI abroad
t: UPI → what it is and how it works
text:
Feature | Fact
Developed by | NPCI (2016)
Regulated by | RBI
Built on | IMPS architecture (real time)
Identifiers | UPI ID/VPA, mobile number, QR code; no account number or IFSC needed
Availability | 24x7, including holidays
Authentication | Device binding + UPI PIN (two-factor)
Interoperability | Any UPI app with any bank; many accounts on one app, one account on many apps
Payments | P2P and P2M
Banks must join UPI; users then pay through PSP/TPAP apps (PhonePe, GPay, Paytm, BHIM)
TPAP (Third-Party Application Provider) needs NPCI approval; works with PSP banks
⚠ Launch date differs: 11 April 2016 (Praveen April 2026, Testbook "April 2016") vs 25 August 2016 (Praveen Aug 2026: public launch); 10 years marked in 2026
## UPI 2.0 (Testbook)
Overdraft accounts linkable; pre-authorised (one-time mandate) payments; signed merchant QR; limit ₹2 lakh/day

topic: UPI, BHIM, wallets and UPI abroad
t: UPI → effect on mobile wallets and digital payments
text:
UPI moves money directly bank-to-bank from a phone: no need to preload a wallet
Option (PYQ 2017) | Verdict
Mobile wallets not necessary for online payments | Correct: likeliest consequence
Digital currency will replace cash in two decades | Wrong: UPI moves bank money, not a new currency
FDI inflows will drastically increase | Wrong: unrelated
Direct transfer of subsidies very effective | Wrong: that is DBT/JAM, not UPI
PYQ 2017: most likely consequence of UPI → mobile wallets will not be necessary; trap: DBT sounds plausible but rides on Aadhaar and accounts
## Shift in usage (PMF)
Debit card volumes fell (495 crore in 2019 to 173 crore in 2024) as users moved to UPI; credit card volume doubled
UPI ≈ 83% of retail digital payments by volume (PMF Payments Vision note)

topic: UPI, BHIM, wallets and UPI abroad
t: Digital wallets (PPIs) → three types
text:
Wallets are Prepaid Payment Instruments (PPIs) regulated by RBI
Type | Use | Cash withdrawal
Closed | Only at the issuing entity (gift card, Ola Money) | No
Semi-closed | Group of contracted merchants (Paytm, PhonePe, Amazon Pay, Mobikwik wallets) | No (transfers allowed)
Open | Issued only by banks; any merchant, transfers | Yes (ATM/PoS)
Since March 2023 NPCI allows wallet interoperability with UPI: pay a UPI QR from a wallet balance
⚠ Only banks can issue open wallets
## Bharat QR
Developed jointly by NPCI, Mastercard and Visa; one interoperable QR, no PoS machine needed; money goes directly to merchant's account

topic: UPI, BHIM, wallets and UPI abroad
t: BHIM → features and authentication
text:
Feature | Fact
Full name | Bharat Interface for Money
By | NPCI, launched December 2016
Based on | UPI
Pays to | Anyone with a UPI-enabled bank account, across banks
Needs | No IFSC or account details
Security | UPI PIN + device binding via SMS
BHIM 2.0 (MeitY): limit for verified merchants raised ₹20,000 to ₹1,00,000 (Testbook)
## Factors of authentication
Instrument | Factors
Chip-PIN debit card | Two: card (possession) + PIN (knowledge)
BHIM/UPI | Two (device + UPI PIN) per PMF; three per Preview (device ID and mobile binding, account sync, app PIN)
⚠ A chip-PIN card does not have four factors: statement 2 is wrong
PYQ 2018: "BHIM lets user pay anyone with a UPI account" → correct; "chip-pin card has four factors, BHIM two" → wrong → answer 1 only

topic: UPI, BHIM, wallets and UPI abroad

text:
Product | What it does
UPI Lite | Small payments without PIN; PMF: up to ₹2,000
UPI Lite X | Offline payments using NFC
UPI 123PAY | UPI on feature phones, no internet
Credit on UPI | RuPay credit cards and pre-sanctioned credit lines on UPI

UPI Tap and Pay | NFC tap, no QR scan
UPI for secondary markets | IPO applications and equity investments

e₹ interoperability | Digital Rupee wallets can pay at UPI QR codes
⚠ UPI Lite still passes through NPCI for verification; only the PIN step is skipped
Credit line on UPI: monthly volume above ₹10,000 crore by mid-2025 (PMF)
## Beyond your notes
RBI raised UPI Lite limits to ₹1,000 per payment and ₹5,000 wallet balance in Dec 2024 (verify; PMF figure ₹2,000 is the older balance cap)

t: UPI abroad → countries where it works

Source and date | Countries

topic: UPI, BHIM, wallets and UPI abroad
t: UPI in numbers → direction of trends
text:
Indicator | Figure
UPI transactions | 1,079 crore (2019) to 17,221 crore (2024): 16-fold (RBI Payment Systems Report)
Global share | India ≈ 48.5-49% of world real-time payments (PMF; IMF via Praveen)
FY 2025-26 | >24,162 crore transactions, ≈ ₹314 lakh crore

QR codes | 709 million active; 23 million soundboxes
Cross-border UPI 2024-25 | 20x volume, 13x value over 2023-24
IMF: UPI is the world's largest real-time retail payment system by volume
⚠ Volume rises but average ticket size falls: do not read rising volume as rising ticket size
## In news 2025-26
Monthly record 2,366 crore transactions worth ₹29.88 lakh crore (July 2026); May 2026: 2,320 crore worth ₹29.90 lakh crore
RBI Digital Payments Index 493.22 (Mar 2025) to 516.76 (Sep 2025)

topic: RTGS, NEFT, IMPS and core banking
t: RTGS vs NEFT → settlement, charges and timing
text:
Feature | RTGS | NEFT
Settlement | Real time, gross (each transaction alone) | Batches (half-hourly), deferred net
Speed | Instant | Some time (up to ~2 hours)
Minimum | ₹2 lakh | No minimum
Maximum | No limit | No limit set by RBI
Use | High-value, urgent, interbank | Small/medium, routine
Operator | RBI | RBI
24x7 since | December 2020 | December 2019
Inward charge to beneficiary | None | None
RBI also abolished charges on outward RTGS/NEFT online transfers (Testbook)
⚠ Neither charges for inward credits: "RTGS charges for inward" is wrong
⚠ Both now 24x7: "RTGS hours restricted but NEFT's are not" is wrong
PYQ 2025: RTGS instant vs NEFT takes time → I only correct; traps: inward charges and operating hours
## In news 2025-26
Pay Point India became the first private fintech to join RBI's Centralised Payment System (RTGS, NEFT) in April 2026; gets own IFSC and RBI accounts

topic: RTGS, NEFT, IMPS and core banking
t: Fund transfer systems → compare RTGS, NEFT, IMPS, UPI
text:
System | Operator | Speed | Limit | Identifier
RTGS | RBI | Real time | Min ₹2 lakh | A/c + IFSC
NEFT | RBI | Batches | None | A/c + IFSC
IMPS | NPCI | Instant 24x7 | ₹5 lakh per txn (RBI cap) | A/c + IFSC, mobile + MMID, Aadhaar
UPI | NPCI | Instant 24x7 | Bank/NPCI-set (see below) | VPA, mobile, QR
NACH | NPCI | Bulk | - | Mandates
MMID = 7-digit Mobile Money Identifier issued per account (Testbook)
NEFT/RTGS are not core India Stack: they serve interbank and institutional flows; India Stack payments layer = UPI
⚠ IMPS (not NEFT) is the base of UPI
## Value and volume trend (RBI Payment Systems Report, PMF Oct 2025)
RTGS leads in value (₹1,938 lakh crore in 2024); UPI leads in volume
NEFT volume tripled to 926.8 crore; IMPS doubled to 593.8 crore (2024)
## Beyond your notes
UPI per-transaction cap is generally ₹1 lakh, higher for some categories such as capital markets, tax and hospitals (verify)

topic: RTGS, NEFT, IMPS and core banking
t: Core Banking Solutions → meaning
text:
CBS = networking of a bank's branches so a customer can operate the account from any branch of that bank, wherever it was opened
Centralised records and software allow access from any location
Statement (PYQ 2016) | Verdict
Networking of branches; operate from any branch | Correct
Effort to increase RBI's control over banks through computerisation | Wrong
Procedure for a bank with huge NPAs taken over by another | Wrong (that is amalgamation/resolution)
PYQ 2016: Core Banking Solutions → 1 only
Jan Dhan accounts are opened as online accounts in banks' core banking systems (Govt Schemes 2026)
Amalgamated RRBs integrated onto unified CBS platforms (Economic Survey 2025-26)
## Beyond your notes
"CORE" is often expanded as Centralised Online Real-time Exchange
CBS is within one bank; interbank transfers need NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI

topic: RTGS, NEFT, IMPS and core banking
t: Money and demand deposits → why bank transfers are money
text:
Modern money = currency + demand deposits (NCERT Class 10)
Cheque = paper instruction to the bank to pay from the account; settles payments without cash
Demand deposits are money because they are accepted widely as a means of payment
Form | Example | Who issues
Currency | Notes and coins | RBI (notes), Govt (coins)
Demand deposits | Savings, current accounts | Commercial banks
Digital rail | NEFT, RTGS, UPI | Moves deposits between banks
CBDC | e₹ | RBI (central bank money)
⚠ UPI/NEFT move bank deposits (commercial bank money); e₹ is central bank money
## In news 2025-26
PM inaugurated RBI Greenfield Data Centre at Jatni, near Bhubaneswar (Odisha), 25 Oct 2026: backup for RBI's Navi Mumbai data centre; secures UPI, NEFT, RTGS continuity

t: MDR → meaning, who pays and who gets it
text:
Merchant Discount Rate = charge paid by the merchant to the bank/payment provider for accepting card or digital payments
Also called Transaction Discount Rate (TDR); % of transaction value
Aspect | Fact
Paid by | Merchant
Collected by | Acquiring bank (merchant's bank) or payment service provider
Shared among | Issuing bank, acquiring bank, PSP bank, network (NPCI/Visa/Mastercard)
Nature | Not a tax, not a government levy
Pre-waiver UPI range | 0.25-0.75%
Covers | Settlement, network fees, infrastructure, app costs
⚠ MDR is not an incentive to merchants, not a refund to customers, not a government subsidy
PYQ 2018: MDR best described as → charge to a merchant by a bank for accepting payments through its debit cards

t: MDR → who sets it and the zero-MDR law
text:
Instrument | Who fixes MDR
Debit cards and regulated instruments | RBI prescribes or caps
UPI | NPCI via its UPI Steering Committee
## Zero MDR (since January 2020)
Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 added Section 10A to the PSS Act, 2007 and Section 269SU in Income Tax Act
No MDR on RuPay debit cards and BHIM-UPI; businesses with turnover ≥₹50 crore must offer RuPay and UPI (Testbook)
Banks bear ≈ ₹0.80 cost per UPI transaction with no MDR (PMF LENS May 2025)
⚠ Testbook says merchants often pass MDR to customers; under the 2026 UPI framework merchants cannot (PMF)
## In news 2025-26
Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Act, 2026 lets the Centre notify modes directly under Section 10A; Finance Ministry notified RuPay debit (no limit) and UPI up to ₹2,000 as charge-free modes (PMF Sep 2026)

t: 2026 UPI MDR framework → rates and exemptions
text:
NPCI revised framework effective 15 October 2026
Transaction | MDR
P2P | Free, any value
P2M up to ₹2,000 | Free
P2PM (small merchants on UPI QR) | Free for monthly receipts up to ₹1 lakh
P2M above ₹2,000 | 0.4%, capped at ₹300 (txns ≥₹75,000)
Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, agri inputs | Flat ₹5 above ₹2,000
Capital-market payments | 0.02%, capped ₹300
Merchants cannot pass MDR to customers; UPI apps cannot levy platform fees
Centre: UPI stays free for consumers (PMF 2027 Q3)
⚠ MDR falls on merchants, never on the payer under this framework

t: Incentive scheme → low-value BHIM-UPI (P2M)
text:
Feature | Fact
Approved | Union Cabinet, for FY 2024-25
Outlay | ₹1,500 crore
Covers | P2M UPI payments up to ₹2,000 by small merchants
Incentive | 0.15% per transaction
Excluded | Payments above ₹2,000; large merchants
Target | Total transaction volume ₹20,000 crore
Paid to | Acquiring bank, shared with issuer bank, PSP bank, app providers (TPAPs)
Disbursal | 80% unconditional each quarter; 20% on performance (10% if technical decline < 0.75%, 10% if uptime > 99.5%)
Zero MDR stays for both small and large merchants
Rural push: Tier 3-6 cities via UPI 123PAY, UPI Lite/Lite X
⚠ Incentive goes to banks, not directly to merchants or customers
P2M = payment from a person's account to a merchant's account; banks charge an interchange fee between themselves

t: Infrastructure funds → PIDF and ADF
text:
Fund | Purpose
Payment Infrastructure Development Fund (PIDF) | RBI fund (on Nilekani Committee advice) to incentivise merchants to deploy PoS
Acceptance Development Fund (ADF) | RBI-set, bank-sponsored fund for the last-mile payment network in Tier III-IV centres
Nandan Nilekani Committee on deepening digital payments: Digital Financial Inclusion Index; 24x7 NEFT; MDR reduction; regional languages
Neeraj Kumar Gupta Committee (April 2016) to boost cashless transactions; after demonetisation a committee under Amitabh Kant (NITI)
⚠ Testbook gives PIDF corpus as ₹500 crore
## Beyond your notes
PIDF began January 2021 (verify extension); Nilekani Committee reported in 2019; RBI's Digital Payments Index has base March 2018 = 100

topic: Data localisation, security and payments policy
t: Payment data localisation → what the RBI rule requires
text:
RBI directive "Storage of Payment System Data", 6 April 2018
Requirement | Fact
Where | Entire payment system data stored only in India
What | Full end-to-end transaction details collected, carried or processed
Who | All payment system providers (incl. foreign: Visa, Mastercard, wallets)
Audit | System Audit Report by CERT-In empanelled auditors
Report to | RBI, by 31 December 2018
⚠ No requirement that systems be owned by public sector enterprises
⚠ Audit report goes to RBI, not CAG
PYQ 2019: correct is only "entire data stored only in India" → 1 only
PMF: RBI's payment data rule is the model for sector-specific localisation
## Beyond your notes
Foreign leg of a cross-border transaction may also be stored abroad; data processed abroad must be brought back within 24 hours (RBI FAQ, June 2019)

topic: Data localisation, security and payments policy
t: Card and account security → EMV, AFA, tokenisation
text:
Term | Meaning
EMV | Europay, Mastercard, Visa chip standard; stops skimming and cloning
AFA | Additional Factor of Authentication (e.g., OTP, PIN)
Switch On/Off | Instantly disable a card; to extend to all methods (Payments Vision 2028)
MMID | 7-digit ID linking a mobile number to an account for IMPS
NFC = short-range (few cm) contactless tech; can use encryption (UPSC 2015)
## Digital Payments E-Mandate Framework, 2026 (RBI)
Under PSS Act, 2007; consolidates rules for cards, UPI, PPIs
One-time registration with AFA; auto-debits up to ₹15,000 without AFA; ₹1 lakh for insurance, mutual funds, credit card bills
No charges for using e-mandates; customer can withdraw anytime
## Beyond your notes
Card tokenisation (RBI, from Oct 2022): merchants cannot store card numbers; a token replaces them (verify)

topic: Data localisation, security and payments policy
t: Digital fraud → RBI compensation framework
text:
Feature | Fact (PMF Feb 2026)
Covers | Small-value digital frauds; targets frauds below ₹50,000 (~65% of cases)
Payout | Up to ₹25,000 or 85% of loss, whichever is lower
Frequency | One-time per customer
Negligence | Covers inadvertent credential sharing if not mala fide
Funding | Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund (~₹85,000 crore)
Burden | Customer 15%, bank ~15%, RBI ~70%
DEA Fund: set up 2014 under Section 26A, Banking Regulation Act
Payments Vision 2028: shared liability of sender's and receiver's banks for unauthorised transactions
⚠ CERT-In: 70% of online financial frauds in 2023 used social engineering

Feature | Fact
What | Consolidates users' financial data from many sources and shares it with consent

t: Digital rupee → features (RBI concept note)
text:
e₹ = India's CBDC: legal tender issued by RBI in digital form; 1 e₹ = 1 ₹ (at par)
Feature | True or false
Sovereign currency issued by RBI in line with monetary policy | True
Liability on RBI's balance sheet | True
Accepted as medium of payment, legal tender, safe store of value | True
Freely convertible with commercial bank money and cash | True
Fungible legal tender; holders need not have a bank account | True
Expected to lower cost of issuing money and transactions | True
Insured against inflation by design | False: loses value with inflation like cash
⚠ Being "1:1 with the rupee" means it carries inflation risk, not protection
PYQ 2024: digital rupee → 1, 2 and 4 correct; trap: "insured against inflation"

t: Digital rupee → types, pilot and wallets
text:
Type | Users
Retail CBDC (e₹-R) | General public: P2P, P2M payments
Wholesale CBDC (e₹-W) | Interbank settlement, financial markets
Launched 2022; in pilot mode, no nationwide rollout yet (PMF S&T)
Held in a digital wallet offered by RBI-authorised banks; cash-like instant settlement, finality; offline use in pilot
e₹ wallets interoperable with UPI QR codes
## Beyond your notes
Announced in Budget 2022-23
Wholesale pilot began 1 November 2022 (government securities settlement); retail pilot 1 December 2022
Legal basis: RBI Act, 1934 amended (Finance Act 2022) to include digital form in "bank note" (verify)

text:
Statement (PYQ 2023) | Verdict
Payments in a digital currency possible without US dollar or SWIFT | Correct: countries can exchange CBDCs bilaterally
Can be distributed with a condition programmed in (e.g., time limit to spend) | Correct: China's e-CNY explores expiry dates
PYQ 2023: both correct → both 1 and 2

CBDC-based Digital Food Currency pilot for PDS in Gujarat: programmable coupons; scan FPS QR
CBDC-based DBT under PM-GKAY in Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli: purpose-bound e₹ tokens in a wallet, usable only for food

t: Cross-border systems → SWIFT and its alternatives
text:
System | Run by | Settles funds?

CIPS | People's Bank of China (2015) | Yes, RMB
SPFS | Bank of Russia (2014) | No, messaging
SEPAM | Central Bank of Iran; linked to SPFS 2023 | No

SWIFT's lead overseer: National Bank of Belgium (with G10); RBI in SWIFT Oversight Forum

t: CBDC vs cryptocurrency vs stablecoin
text:
Aspect | CBDC (e₹) | Cryptocurrency | Stablecoin
Issuer | Central bank | Private, decentralised | Private firm
Legal tender | Yes | No | No
Value | Stable (fiat 1:1) | Highly volatile | Pegged to asset (e.g., USD)
Regulation | Fully regulated | Largely unregulated | Varies
Ledger | Central (can use DLT) | Blockchain | Blockchain
Stablecoins: Tether (USDT) and USDC ≈ 90% of a $285 bn market (IMF 2025); Economic Survey 2025-26: $305.4 bn
India does not recognise stablecoins; all crypto = VDAs (Sec 2(47A), IT Act 1961)
⚠ Programmability exists in both CBDC and tokens; only CBDC has legal tender status
## In news 2025-26
RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra (IMF-World Bank meetings, Oct 2025) urged central banks to prefer CBDCs over stablecoins for cross-border payments: risk of rupee dollarisation
US GENIUS Act on stablecoins passed the Senate

t: CBDC in news → global and bilateral moves
text:
Development | Detail
BRICS CBDC linkage | RBI proposed linking BRICS CBDCs: pay foreign merchants without converting to USD (LENS Jan 2026)
India's stance | Opposes a single BRICS currency (would dilute monetary independence)
India-UAE | Frameworks to test interoperable CBDCs; UPI-UAE IPP linkage; RuPay with UAESWITCH (Oct 2026)
Global | Only 19 central banks with pilot-stage CBDCs (IMF tracker 2025); >60% cite cyber risk (BIS)
Cost | CBDCs can cut remittance costs ~50% vs SWIFT (BIS 2025)
Tokenised CBDC = central bank money as blockchain tokens: instant, programmable, traceable
Only 26% of Indians understand CBDC basics (FIS 2024)
⚠ Tokenised CBDC is still legal tender; a stablecoin is not

t: Bitcoin → features
text:
Statement (PYQ 2016) | Verdict
Bitcoins are tracked by central banks | Wrong: decentralised, no central authority
Anyone with a Bitcoin address can send/receive with anyone else | Correct: peer-to-peer
Payments without either side knowing the identity of the other | Correct: pseudonymous
PYQ 2016: Bitcoin → 2 and 3 only
## Basics
Created 2009 by pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto; first decentralised crypto
Supply capped at 21 million coins; new coins by mining (solving puzzles to validate blocks)
Runs on blockchain: decentralised, tamper-resistant distributed ledger
⚠ "Anonymous" = pseudonymous: addresses are public on the ledger, identities are not

text:
Asset | Feature
Bitcoin (BTC) | First (2009); 21 million cap
Ethereum (ETH) | Smart contracts, dApps; native coin Ether
Litecoin (LTC) | Faster block time; small quick payments
Ripple (XRP) | Fast, low-cost cross-border payments
Bitcoin Cash (BCH) | Hard fork of Bitcoin (2017), bigger blocks

Stablecoin | Pegged to fiat/asset
VDA = digitally stored, transferable representation of value, not backed by a government (PMF)

t: India's crypto policy → timeline
text:
Year | Step
2013 | RBI first warns on virtual currencies
2018 | RBI circular bars banks from serving crypto businesses
2020 | SC (IMAI v. RBI) quashes circular: violates Art 19(1)(g)
2021 | Draft bill: ban private crypto, prepare for CBDC
2022 | 30% tax on VDA income + 1% TDS per transfer; RBI starts e₹ pilots
2023 | VDAs under PMLA 2002; exchanges register with FIU-IND (KYC, AML)
2025 | Income Tax Act, 2025 classifies VDAs as property and capital assets
Crypto is legal to hold and trade but not legal tender

t: Crypto taxation → rules
text:
Rule | Fact
Tax on gains | 30% flat (Budget 2022)
TDS | 1% on each transfer
Loss set-off | One crypto's loss cannot offset another's gain
Carry forward | Losses cannot be carried forward
Gifts | Taxable at slab rates above ₹50,000

t: Market → money market or capital market
text:
## 1. The dividing line
Money market = short-term funds, up to 364 days (Testbook); regulated by RBI
Capital market = long-term funds, beyond 364 days; regulated by SEBI
Market / instrument | Segment
Call / notice money | Money market
Treasury bills (91, 182, 364 days) | Money market
Cash Management Bills (<91 days) | Money market
Commercial Paper, Certificate of Deposit | Money market
CBLO (CCIL, 2003), repo | Money market
Government bond (dated G-sec) market | Capital market
Stock (share) market, debentures, corporate bonds | Capital market
⚠ T-bills are G-secs but sit in the money market; dated G-secs sit in the capital market
⚠ RBI is not a participant in the money market; it only manages liquidity through LAF (Preview)
PYQ 2023: how many of four markets are capital markets: only two (G-bond and stock); call money and T-bill markets are money market
PYQ 2024: CBLO is a money market instrument, not bond, forex or stock market

t: Money market instruments → issuer, tenure, security
text:
## 1. Five instruments UPSC pairs
Instrument | Issued by | Tenure | Key feature
Commercial Paper (1990) | Corporates, Primary Dealers, AIFIs | 7 days - 1 year | Unsecured promissory note; needs credit rating
Certificate of Deposit (1989) | SCBs (not RRBs, LABs) and select AIFIs | Short term (<1 yr for banks) | Negotiable, demat; not issued by RBI
Call money | Banks and PDs, lend/borrow | Overnight (notice: 2-14 days) | Interbank; most volatile segment
Treasury Bill | GoI only (via RBI) | 91/182/364 days | Zero coupon, issued at discount
CBLO | CCIL platform | Short term | Collateralised by securities such as T-bills
⚠ CD is short-term and bank-issued: "long-term instrument issued by RBI to a corporation" is the 2020 trap
⚠ Zero-coupon bonds pay no interest; sold at deep discount, redeemed at face value
FIs (IFCI, IDBI, EXIM) may issue CDs of 1-3 years (Testbook)
## Beyond your notes
CBLO was replaced by TREPS (tri-party repo) in 2018 (verify)
PYQ 2020: CP (short-term unsecured) and call money (interbank) correct; CD and zero-coupon statements wrong

t: Organised money market → origin and players
text:
## 1. Committees and history (Testbook)
Item | Fact
Chakravarthy Committee (1985) | Need for an organised money market
Vaghul Committee (1987) | Blueprint for the organised money market
DFHI (Apr 1988) | RBI + PSBs + LIC, GIC, UTI; chief market-maker; now SBI DFHI, largest primary dealer
Treasury Bills | Formalised 1986; 14-day variants dropped 2001
CMB (Aug 2009) | <91 days; not under Ways and Means Advances; SLR-eligible
Commercial Bill | 1990; replaced old Bill Market (1952)
Money Market Mutual Funds | 1992; under SEBI since March 2000 (with RBI)
Repo / reverse repo | Dec 1992 / Nov 1996; term repo 2014 on Urjit Patel panel
## 2. Unorganised money market
Chit funds, nidhis (lend to members, South India), loan companies: 36-48% interest
Indigenous bankers: Gujarati Shroffs, Multani/Shikarpuri Shroffs, Marwari Kayas, Chettiars (Chennai)
Money lenders: professional and non-professional
⚠ T-bills also count for banks' SLR; RBI is regulator, not a money-market participant

t: Primary vs secondary market → meaning
text:
## 1. Two parts of the capital market (Testbook)
Point | Primary market | Secondary market
Deals in | New securities | Already issued securities
Money goes to | Issuer (company, govt) | Selling investor
Routes | IPO, FPO, rights issue, private placement | Stock exchanges
Function | Capital formation | Liquidity, price discovery
## 2. Issue terms
Term | Meaning
Book building | Investors bid within a price band; price set by bids
Shares at premium | Price above face value; firms with 5-year profit record
Private placement | Sold to a few investors (>50 investors brings SEBI in, Sahara case)
Grey market | Unofficial pre-listing trade; SEBI plans a "when-listed" platform (PMF)
Sweat equity | Shares to employees/directors for know-how
⚠ Retail buying in an RBI G-sec auction via Retail Direct is a primary market purchase

t: Gilt-edged market → meaning
text:
## 1. Gilt-edged = government securities
Gilt-edged market = market for government securities: interest and redemption are certain
G-secs carry practically no default risk → "risk-free gilt-edged instruments" (PMF)
Gilt fund = mutual fund investing in G-secs; Retail Direct Gilt (RDG) account = retail G-sec account
Term | Means | Not
Gilt-edged | Govt securities | Bullion, pure metals
Blue chip | Shares of large, consistently profitable firms | Govt-guaranteed shares
Penny stock | Low-priced, volatile shares | Blue chip
⚠ "Gilt" is not gold: options like bullion market are the trap
PYQ 2000: gilt-edged market = market of government securities

t: G-secs → who issues what, who manages
text:
## 1. Types of G-secs (PMF)
Feature | T-Bills | Dated G-secs / SDLs
Maturity | Less than 1 year | 1 year or more (5-40 years)
Issued by | Central Government only | Centre (dated G-sec) and States (SDLs)
Interest | Zero coupon, issued at discount, redeemed at par | Fixed/floating coupon, half-yearly
CMBs: GoI, maturity <91 days, temporary cash mismatches (since 2009)
Issued by RBI through auction on E-Kuber; RBI's Public Debt Office is registry/depository
## 2. RBI manages both
RBI manages Central and State debt (Sec 21A RBI Act, by agreement with each State; all except Sikkim, which has a limited agreement)
⚠ "RBI manages GoI securities but not State securities" is false
⚠ States issue no T-bills: only SDLs
PYQ 2018: correct = only GoI issues T-bills; T-bills issued at a discount

t: G-sec market → who can buy, trade and hold
text:
## 1. Participants
Participant | Access
Retail investors | Primary and secondary market via RBI Retail Direct (launched 12 Nov 2021; RDG account; mobile app)
Insurance cos, pension funds | Trade corporate bonds and G-secs
FIIs/FPIs | Can hold G-secs within limits: 6% of Central G-secs, 2% of SGSs
Primary Dealers (NBFCs) | Can access RBI's LAF
Stock exchanges | Can run separate debt trading platforms (NSE's first, 2013)
NDS-OM = RBI-owned screen-based anonymous order-matching system for secondary G-sec trading
CDSL (1999) was promoted by BSE, later divested to banks: not RBI
⚠ Official key 2024: all three LAF/FII/debt-platform statements correct (PDs are NBFCs); Preview's key marks the NBFC-LAF line wrong
PYQ 2024: insurance cos, pension funds and retail investors can all trade corporate bonds and G-secs
## In news 2025-26
From 1 Apr 2026 FPIs exempt from tax on G-sec interest and capital gains; FAR now covers new 15/30/40-year G-secs and sovereign green bonds (PMF)

t: Bond yields → what moves them
text:
## 1. Yield and price move inversely
Bond yield = return given coupon and market price; price up → yield down (PMF)
Driver | Effect on Indian G-sec yields
RBI policy rate hike | Short-term yields rise
US Fed raising US yields | FPIs shift to US assets → Indian yields rise
Inflation, short-term rates | Higher inflation expectations → yields rise
Higher govt borrowing | More G-sec supply → yields rise
Rising yields: costlier govt borrowing, crowding out of private investment, valuation losses for banks, more FPI debt inflow
⚠ All three (Fed, RBI, inflation) influence yields: "RBI only" is the trap
PYQ 2021: answer 1, 2 and 3
## In news 2025-26
10-year G-sec yield hit a two-year high of 7.21% on 1 Oct 2026 (PMF LENS)
RBI OMO sale auctions of ₹1 lakh crore (Sept 2026) to absorb liquidity (PMF)

t: Corporate bond market → size and reforms
text:
## 1. Status (Economic Survey 2025-26)
Indicator | Figure
Corporate bonds / GDP (Mar 2025) | ~15-16%
Peers | South Korea 79%, Malaysia 54%, China 38%
Skew | 85-90% of issuance by AAA issuers; PSUs, PFIs, banks dominate
Debt share of primary mobilisation (Apr-Dec 2025) | >63%
## 2. Reforms (Testbook, RBI after Khan Committee 2016)
BBB declared investment grade (earlier AA); partial credit enhancement by banks raised to 50%
Corporate bonds eligible collateral in LAF; electronic repo platform; CDS on unlisted rated bonds, CPs, CDs
Pension, provident funds and insurers may invest in corporate bonds; Masala bonds by banks
## In news 2025-26
Budget 2026-27: market-making framework, derivatives on corporate bond indices, total return swaps; TReDS receivables as asset-backed securities
SEBI ESG debt framework (social, sustainability, sustainability-linked bonds); municipal bond outreach

t: Inflation-Indexed Bonds → features and tax
text:
## 1. IIBs (Testbook, Preview)
Return = fixed real rate + inflation compensation; protect principal and interest
Feature | Fact
Earlier version | Capital Indexed Bonds (1997): protected principal only
June 2013 IIB | Linked to WPI; tepid retail response
Dec 2013 IINSS-C | Linked to CPI (3-month lag), fixed rate 1.5%, 10 years
For investors | Protection from inflation uncertainty
For government | Lower coupon (no inflation-risk premium)
Tax | No special treatment: interest and capital gains taxable
⚠ "Interest and capital gains on IIBs are not taxable" is false
PYQ 2022: correct = 1 and 2 only (lower coupon for govt; protection for investors)

t: Gold schemes → objective
text:
## 1. Sovereign Gold Bond and Gold Monetisation Scheme (2015)
Scheme | What | Status
Sovereign Gold Bond | Issued by RBI on behalf of GoI; fixed interest + gold-price gain | Fresh issuance discontinued (PMF, 2025)
Gold Monetisation Scheme | Deposit idle gold; replaced Gold Deposit and Gold Metal Loan schemes | Medium (5-7 yr) and long-term (12-15 yr) deposits discontinued (Mar 2025); short-term bank deposit (1-3 yr) continues
Shared objectives: mobilise idle household gold, cut gold imports (helps CAD)

Gold ETF: one unit ≈ 1 gram of gold, exchange-listed, SEBI norms; EGR = exchange-traded gold receipt

t: Green and thematic bonds → features
text:
## 1. Bonds in news (PMF)
Bond | Feature
Sovereign Green Bond | Budget 2022-23; proceeds only for green public infrastructure; FIIs allowed to invest; in FAR
Blue bond | Finances ocean and water projects; SMFCL plans India's first; first sovereign: Seychelles 2018

t: Bondholder vs shareholder → risk and status
text:
## 1. Lender vs owner
Point | Bondholder / debenture holder | Shareholder
Status | Lender = creditor | Owner
Return | Contractual fixed interest + principal | Dividend + price change (uncertain)
Repayment priority | First (also in liquidation) | Residual claim
Risk | Lower | Higher
Debenture = medium/long-term debt certificate of a company at fixed interest
OFCDs: option to convert debentures into shares; Sahara case → SEBI got jurisdiction over any scheme with 50+ investors (Companies Amendment 2012)
⚠ Debenture holders are creditors, not shareholders, debtors or directors
PYQ 2025 (Statement I-II-III): II (lenders vs owners) and III (repaid first) both correct and both explain I (lower risk)

t: Convertible and zero-coupon bonds → features
text:
## 1. Bond variants
Bond | Feature
Convertible bond | Can convert into fixed number of shares; lower coupon because of the equity option
Zero-coupon bond | No interest; deep discount, redeemed at face value
ZCZP (Social Stock Exchange) | No interest, no principal; issued by NPOs; a security under SCRA 1956
Infra bond vs InvIT | Debt, fixed return vs trust, market-linked distributions
Conversion option gives the holder some indexation to rising prices (equity can rise with inflation)

t: Masala bonds → issuer and denomination
text:
## 1. Masala bond
Rupee-denominated bond issued outside India to overseas investors; currency risk lies with the investor
Name coined by IFC (World Bank Group arm) to evoke Indian culture and cuisine (PMF)
First Masala bond by IFC, Nov 2014: ₹1,000 crore for Indian infrastructure
Luxembourg Stock Exchange first to list Masala bonds (PMF)
Source of debt finance for public and private sector; Indian banks allowed to issue them for infra and affordable housing (Testbook)
Bond | Currency | Market
Masala | Indian rupee | Abroad
ECB / foreign-currency bond | Foreign currency | Abroad
Panda / Samurai | Yuan / Yen | China / Japan (foreign issuers)
⚠ Encouraging Masala bonds helps stop a rupee slide (PYQ 2019 angle)
PYQ 2016: both statements correct (IFC = World Bank arm; rupee-denominated debt)
## Beyond your notes
Panda and Samurai bond pairs (verify before use)

t: Participatory Notes → who issues to whom
text:
## 1. P-Notes / ODIs (PMF)
Issued by registered FPIs to overseas investors who invest in Indian stocks without registering with SEBI
Underlying asset: Indian stocks; they are Overseas Derivative Instruments
Due diligence (KYC) is mandatory; criticised as opaque, made more transparent by SEBI monitoring
Term | Meaning
FII | Institutional investors: insurers, pension funds, sovereign wealth funds
FPI | Wider group: includes individuals and FIIs
ODI | P-note: derivative on Indian assets issued abroad

PYQ 2019: P-notes issued by registered FPIs; PYQ 2007: associated with FIIs
## In news 2025-26
IFSCA lets non-bank entities such as AIFs issue ODIs from IFSC; IFSC banks may issue ODIs (PMF)

t: Financial instrument → yes or no
text:
## 1. What counts
Financial instrument = contract with monetary value that can be traded, created or settled
Item | Financial instrument?
Stocks, bonds, mutual fund units, ETFs | Yes
Derivatives: futures, options, swaps (incl. currency swap) | Yes
Cheques, CDs, deposits, loans | Yes
Motor vehicles | No: tangible asset (a vehicle loan is one)

t: Derivatives → types and regulator
text:
## 1. Main contracts (PMF)
Derivative | Feature
Forward | Private, customised contract
Futures | Exchange-traded obligation to buy/sell at fixed price on future date
Options | Right, not obligation; Call = right to buy, Put = right to sell; buyer pays premium
Swap | Exchange of cash flows: interest-rate, currency swap
CDS | Buyer pays premium; seller pays on default; naked CDS fed the 2008 crisis
Non-deliverable derivative | Cash-settled in USD offshore (Singapore, London)
Exchange F&O regulated by SEBI under SCRA 1956; commodity derivatives also SEBI (after FMC merger)

Weather derivatives: NCDEX-IMD MoU (India's first); electricity futures launched on NSE (SEBI-CERC)

t: Foreign portfolio investors → categories, routes and limits
text:
## 1. FPI basics
India opened to FPI/FII in 1994; FPIs invest in equity, debt, derivatives without seeking control
FPI is the wider group (includes individuals); FII = institutions (insurers, pension funds, SWFs)
SEBI category (Testbook) | Who
I | Govt and govt-related entities, central banks
II | Regulated entities: banks, mutual funds, insurers
III | Others
## 2. Routes into G-secs (PMF)
Route | Feature
General route | Overall caps: 6% of Central G-secs, 2% of State securities
Fully Accessible Route (FAR) | Select G-secs without limits; now incl. 15/30/40-yr bonds, green bonds
## In news 2025-26
SWAFAT-FI single window for trusted FPIs (sovereign funds, regulated public retail funds); India Market Access portal (SEBI)
FPIs net sellers in FY26; DII holding in NSE firms (18.7%) overtook FII share for the first time (Econ Survey)

t: Alternative Investment Funds → which category
text:
## 1. AIF basics
Privately pooled investment vehicle under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012; distinct from mutual funds
Category | Invests in | Example
I | Start-ups, SMEs, socially beneficial sectors | Venture capital funds, angel funds, Social Impact Funds
II | Private equity, debt, unlisted cos, no leverage | PE funds
III | Complex trading strategies | Hedge funds
⚠ Bonds (debt securities) and stocks (units of ownership) are not AIFs
FPIs may invest up to 25% in Category III AIFs (Testbook)
Social Impact Fund: Cat I sub-category, min corpus ₹5 crore (others ₹20 crore)
PYQ 2025: of bonds, hedge funds, stocks, venture capital → only two are AIFs
## In news 2025-26
New AIF category only for accredited investors (SEBI, Sept 2025); AIFs can be declared "inoperative" (2026)
GARUDA green-channel proposal: AIF launch for non-accredited investors in 10 working days (from 30)

t: Mutual funds and ETFs → structure and types
text:
## 1. Structure (Testbook)
Pool money from many investors; run by an AMC; overseen by a board of trustees; regulated by SEBI
Units priced at NAV (total investment value / units), disclosed daily; NFO price usually ₹10
Scheme | Feature

## 1. The rule
Type | Test | Examples

## 1. The definitions
Deficit | Formula
Revenue deficit | Revenue expenditure − revenue receipts
Effective revenue deficit | Revenue deficit − grants for creation of capital assets
Fiscal deficit | Total expenditure − total receipts excluding borrowings = total borrowing
Primary deficit | Fiscal deficit − interest payments
Budget deficit (old) | Total expenditure − total receipts (incl. borrowings)
Monetised deficit | Part of deficit financed by RBI buying govt securities
Fiscal deficit = borrowing requirement of the government

## 1. The logic
Concept | Counts borrowing as receipt? | Size
Budget deficit | Yes (gap after all receipts) | Smaller
Fiscal deficit | No (receipts exclude borrowing) | Larger - equals all borrowing + other liabilities
Budget deficit was financed by ad hoc T-bills (RBI); the concept lost use after ad hoc T-bills ended (1997)
## Beyond your notes
Ways and Means Advances (WMA) replaced ad hoc T-bills from April 1997; budget deficit stopped being reported thereafter

Given | Value
Revenue expenditure | 80,000
Revenue receipts | 60,000
Borrowings | 10,000
Interest | 6,000
RD = 80,000 − 60,000 | 20,000
FD = borrowings | 10,000
PD = 10,000 − 6,000 | 4,000
## 2. Gross primary deficit problem
FD 50,000; non-debt capital receipts 10,000; interest 1,500
Gross PD = FD − interest = 48,500

## 1. Drill A
Item | ₹ crore
Revenue receipts | 1,000
Revenue expenditure | 1,300 (incl. interest 200; capital-asset grants 100)
Capital expenditure | 400
Non-debt capital receipts | 100
## 2. Answers
Deficit | Working | Result
Revenue deficit | 1,300 − 1,000 | 300
Effective RD | 300 − 100 | 200
Fiscal deficit | (1,300 + 400) − (1,000 + 100) | 600

t: Fiscal stimulus → which measures count
text:
## 1. Expansionary vs contractionary
Expansionary (stimulus) | Contractionary
Cut taxes | Raise taxes
Raise government spending, public works | Abolish/cut subsidies
Bigger transfers | Cut spending
Fiscal stimulus = intense government action (spending, tax cuts) to boost economic activity
In a recession: increase spending on public projects (multiplier, capex)
Testbook: deficits can stimulate growth short-term, but sustained deficits raise debt, interest and inflation
Countercyclical policy: deficits in downturns, consolidation in booms
⚠ Abolishing subsidies cuts demand - it is not a stimulus
PYQ 2010: stimulus = tax cuts + higher spending; PYQ 2011: stimulus = intense govt action to boost activity
PYQ 2021: in a recession govt is most likely to increase public project spending (not cut taxes on luxuries or raise interest rates)

topic: Fiscal policy: stimulus, deficit control, crowding out
t: Fiscal vs monetary policy → who uses which tool
text:
## 1. Tools
Policy | Authority | Tools
Fiscal | Government (Finance Ministry, Parliament) | Taxes, spending, borrowing, subsidies
Monetary | RBI (MPC) | Repo rate, CRR, SLR, OMO, VRR auctions
## 2. Recession vs inflation response
Situation | Fiscal | Monetary
Recession | Raise spending, cut taxes | Cut repo, cut CRR, buy G-secs (OMO)
Inflation | Cut spending, raise taxes | Raise repo, sell G-secs
RBI OMO purchases of G-secs inject liquidity; RBI also manages the govt's borrowing programme (earns a management commission)
Automatic stabilisers: progressive taxes and welfare payments rise/fall with the cycle
⚠ Raising interest rates is monetary and contractionary - wrong answer for a recession question
## Beyond your notes
Fiscal multiplier: capex has a higher multiplier than revenue spending (transfers, subsidies)

topic: Fiscal policy: stimulus, deficit control, crowding out
t: Crowding out vs crowding in → effect of govt borrowing
text:
## 1. Two effects
Effect | Mechanism
Crowding out | Govt borrowing → higher interest rates → less private investment
Crowding in | Good-quality public capex raises returns → draws in private investment
P-MCA 2025: crowding out = government spending discourages private investment
Heavy G-sec issuance also crowds out the corporate bond market (Testbook)
⚠ Crowding out works through interest rates / loanable funds, not through taxes
PYQ 2026: crowding out = borrowing raises interest rates, reducing private investment
## In news 2025-26
Economic Survey 2025-26: better-quality capex (effective capex 4% of GDP in FY25) promotes crowding-in; states' unconditional cash transfers are crowding out capex

topic: Fiscal policy: stimulus, deficit control, crowding out
t: Reducing the deficit → which steps work
text:
## 1. Measures
Reduces deficit | Does not
Cut revenue expenditure | New welfare schemes (add spending)
Rationalise subsidies | Encouraging FDI (private flow, not budget)
Downsize bureaucracy | Privatising higher education (not a fiscal lever)
Disinvestment (sell PSU shares) | Expanding industries (indirect)
Better tax collection, asset monetisation | -
Economic Survey 2025-26: DBT prevented ₹3.48 lakh crore of leakages in a decade
16th FC: subsidies need sunset clauses and exclusion criteria; cash transfers = 20.2% of subsidy spending (2025-26), up from 3% (2018-19)
⚠ Disinvestment reduces the fiscal deficit (non-debt capital receipt) but not the revenue deficit
PYQ 2015: reduce revenue expenditure + rationalise subsidies (1 and 3)
PYQ 2010: downsizing bureaucracy and selling PSU shares (3 and 4 only)

topic: Fiscal policy: stimulus, deficit control, crowding out
t: Deficit financing → purpose and effects
text:
## 1. Key points
Deficit financing = covering the gap by borrowing (and, historically, money creation)
In India it was used to raise resources for economic development (plans, 1950s-70s)
Effects: inflation if monetised (more money vs goods), debt build-up, higher interest burden
Phase | Feature
1950s-60s | Plans; low tax base, weak banks, low savings
1970s-80s | Rising deficits, oil shocks
1991 | Crisis; reforms, fiscal consolidation
⚠ Assertion "deficit financing leads to inflation" - true, because money supply rises relative to goods
PYQ 2013: deficit financing in India is used for economic development (not for paying debt or BoP)

text:

Indicator | Trend
Fiscal deficit | 9.2% (FY21) → 4.8% (FY25) → 4.4% (FY26) → 4.3% (BE FY27)
Revenue deficit | Lowest since FY09 (FY25)
Revenue receipts | ~9.1% of GDP post-pandemic
Direct tax share | Rising
Effective capex | 4% of GDP (FY25)
Neither tax-GDP nor FD-GDP rose steadily; both fluctuated (FD spiked 2008-09 and 2020-21)

t: Internal debt → its components
text:
## 1. Composition
Internal debt item | Note
Dated securities (G-secs) | Market-related rates, auctions; largest part
Treasury bills | 91, 182, 364 days; also 14-day intermediate T-bills (non-marketable)
Special securities to RBI | (Historic ad hoc T-bills, converted)
Securities against small savings (NSSF) | Household savings route
Securities to IFIs | IMF, World Bank, ADB contributions
Compensation and other bonds | -
Public debt = liabilities on the Consolidated Fund; other liabilities = Public Account (provident funds, reserve funds, deposits)
Marketable debt ≈ 64-65% of central liabilities; non-marketable = 14-day ITBs, small-savings securities, bonds to PSBs/EXIM, IFI securities
External debt of the Centre = loans from multilaterals (IMF, World Bank, ADB), bilateral loans from foreign governments

t: Household savings and government borrowing → the link
text:
## 1. How savings fund debt
Channel | How
Small savings (NSC, PPF) | Credited to NSSF, invested in special G-secs
Bank deposits | Banks hold G-secs (SLR 18%; actual ~26%)
Insurance, PF, pension funds | Invest in G-secs
So a share of household financial savings goes to government borrowing
Household financial savings include currency, deposits, debt securities, mutual funds, PF and pension funds, insurance and small savings (Preview)
Bank deposits get 40% or less of household savings now (down from 50%) as money moves to mutual funds and pensions (LENS Feb 2025)
Dated securities at market rates in auctions = largest component of internal debt

Net household savings at a five-decade low; liabilities up 102% since 2019-20 vs assets 48% (LENS Nov 2025)

t: G-sec instruments → features
text:
## 1. Types
Instrument | Feature
T-bills | Zero-coupon, issued at discount, 91/182/364 days; Centre only
Cash Management Bills | Under 91 days, temporary mismatches
Dated securities | Fixed or floating coupon, long tenor
SDLs | States issue only dated securities (no T-bills)
Issued by RBI through auction on E-Kuber; RBI Public Debt Office is registry; "gilt-edged", practically no default risk
Bond price and yield move inversely
## In news 2025-26
G-sec reforms (from 1 April 2026): FPIs exempt from tax on interest and capital gains on G-secs; FAR extended to new 15, 30, 40-year G-secs and sovereign green bonds; overall FPI limits stay 6% (Central) and 2% (State) (Prelims Magnum 2027 Q2)

t: Debt sustainability → debt trap and risk metrics
text:
## 1. Terms
Term | Meaning
Debt trap | Borrowing to pay interest on outstanding loans
Golden rule | Borrow only for capital assets, not salaries or subsidies
Rollover risk | Debt maturing at once; reduced by switches and buybacks
IP/RR ratio | Interest payments ÷ revenue receipts
Central debt profile: weighted average maturity of new issues ~19 years, stock 13.66 years; floating-rate debt 4.1%; external debt ~2.6% of GDP (mostly concessional)
⚠ Debt trap ≠ IMF conditionality or loan refusal
PYQ 2002: debt trap = having to borrow to pay interest
## In news 2025-26
General govt debt-GDP down ~7.1 percentage points since 2020 (Economic Survey 2025-26)
⚠ LENS July 2026 says general government debt is above 80% of GDP (rating view); Survey stresses the fall since 2020

t: Disinvestment → types and use of proceeds
text:

Type | Feature
Disinvestment (minority) | Sell <50% stake; govt keeps control
Strategic disinvestment | Sell 50% or more + transfer of management control (privatisation)
Asset monetisation | Lease or recycle assets (e.g., REITs)
Proceeds = non-debt capital receipt; cut the fiscal deficit
Disinvestment does not necessarily mean giving up management control
## Beyond your notes
Proceeds go to the Consolidated Fund; used for capital spending and social sector (NIF), not mainly to repay external debt
⚠ Both 2011 statements were false: not mainly for external debt; control not necessarily surrendered
PYQ 2011: neither statement correct
## In news 2025-26
Strategic disinvestment: 36 CPSEs approved since 2016, 13 completed (Economic Survey 2025-26)

t: Redistribution of income → which tax-spending mix
text:
## 1. The tested answer
Combination | Effect on inequality
Progressive taxation + progressive expenditure | Best redistribution (the answer)
Progressive taxation + regressive expenditure | Gains from the tax side are undone by spending
Regressive taxation + progressive expenditure | Poor pay more of the tax, then get it back
Regressive taxation + regressive expenditure | Widens inequality
Progressive tax: the average tax burden rises with income; high-income families pay a disproportionately high share
Progressive expenditure: spending that favours the poor (free medical aid, free education, subsidised housing)
Principle for spending: maximum social welfare
PMF: growth driven by direct taxes reduces inequality through progressive redistribution
⚠ Redistribution needs both halves; progressive taxation alone is not the answer UPSC wanted
PYQ 1996: four tax-spending combinations; answer progressive taxation with progressive expenditure

t: Progressive, proportional, regressive, degressive → meaning
text:
## 1. The four tax shapes
Type | Rate as income rises | Example
Progressive | Rate rises | Income tax in India (slabs)
Proportional | Rate stays the same | A flat-rate tax
Regressive | Burden falls as a share of income | Indirect taxes (same rate for all income groups)
Degressive | Rises at first, then flat at the top | India's tax system overall
PMF: a higher direct-to-indirect tax ratio is considered more progressive
Indirect taxes are called regressive because the rich and poor pay the same rate on the same good
⚠ India's income tax is progressive; the system as a whole is described as degressive (Uttarakhand PCS 2021 key)
⚠ Income tax is a direct tax collected by the Union, not by the States

t: Direct vs indirect taxes → definition and examples
text:
## 1. The test: who bears the burden
Feature | Direct tax | Indirect tax
Burden | Borne by the person taxed; cannot be shifted | Shifted to the final consumer
Base | Income, profits, wealth, property | Goods and services (consumption)
Examples | Income tax, corporation tax, capital gains tax, STT, property tax, death duties | GST, customs, excise, old sales tax/VAT, service tax
Administered (Centre) | CBDT | CBIC
## 2. Classify-these (NCERT exercise)
Direct: property tax, death duties, income tax
Indirect: sales tax, customs duties, VAT
⚠ STT is a direct tax (CBDT, counted in direct tax collections); MOSPI classifies it as indirect, because the broker pays it
⚠ Equalisation levy was also classed as a direct tax by PMF
## In news 2025-26
Economic Survey 2025-26: share of direct taxes in total taxes 58.8% in FY25, average 55.5% in FY22-FY25
Union Budget 2026-27 (BE): direct taxes 6.9% of GDP, indirect taxes 4.3%

t: Types of direct taxes → what each covers
text:
## 1. Central direct taxes
Tax | Key fact
Income tax | Individuals, HUFs, firms, co-operatives, trusts, artificial juridical persons; progressive
Corporation tax | Profits of companies incorporated in India or wholly controlled from India
MAT | Finance Act 1987, for "zero-tax" companies; dropped 1990-91, back 1996-97; on book profit
AMT | Same idea as MAT for non-corporate taxpayers (individuals, firms, LLPs)
DDT | On dividends paid by companies; abolished from 1 April 2020 (now taxed with the shareholder)
STT | On trades in listed securities; 2004
Income tax and corporation tax are levied under the Income Tax Act, 1961 (replaced by the Income-tax Act, 2025 from 1 April 2026)
CBDT: statutory body under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963, Department of Revenue; members from the IRS (IT)

## Beyond your notes
Wealth tax abolished from 2015-16 (replaced by a surcharge on the super-rich)

t: Articles 268-271 → who levies, collects, appropriates
text:
## 1. The distribution scheme (after the 80th and 101st Amendments)
Article | Levied by | Collected and kept by | Taxes
268 | Union | States | Stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques, promissory notes, insurance policies, share transfers
269 | Union | Union collects, assigned to States | Inter-state sale (other than newspapers) and consignment of goods
269A | Union | Shared Union-States on GST Council advice | IGST on inter-state supplies
270 | Union | Union collects, shared with States (Finance Commission) | All Union List taxes except 268, 269, 269A, surcharges, cesses
271 | Union | Union only | Surcharges on Art 269 and 270 taxes
Art 268A (service tax, 88th Amendment 2003) and Entry 92C were removed by the 101st Amendment
80th Amendment (2000): "Alternative Scheme of Devolution" of the 10th Finance Commission (29% of central taxes to States)
⚠ A surcharge cannot be imposed on GST
⚠ Income tax falls under Art 270: Union levies, collects and shares it; only the surcharge stays with the Union
PYQ 1999: Union levies, collects and distributes income tax between itself and the States; trap option said only the surcharge is shared, which is the reverse

t: Union List and State List tax entries → which government taxes what
text:
## 1. Union List (List I, Entries 82-92B, 13 entries)
Income tax (other than agricultural income), corporation tax, customs, central excise
Taxes on transactions in stock exchanges and futures markets (other than stamp duties)
Entry 97: residuary taxing power belongs to the Union only
## 2. State List (List II, Entries 45-63, 18 entries)
State tax | Note
Agricultural income tax | Only States can tax farm income
Land revenue | State tax
State excise on alcohol for human consumption | Outside GST
Entertainment and amusement taxes | Mostly into GST; local-body levies stay
Taxes on professions | Cap ₹2,500 a year per person (Art 276)
Sale or consumption of electricity | Not on electricity used by or sold to the Centre (Art 287)
## 3. Concurrent List
No tax entries; GST is a concurrent power created by the 101st Amendment (Art 246A), not a List III entry
⚠ Testbook lists GST and stamp duties under "Concurrent" for convenience; the Constitution's List III has no tax entry
## Beyond your notes
Entry 82 (List I): taxes on income other than agricultural income; Entry 46 (List II): taxes on agricultural income

t: Stock exchange and futures transactions → levied and collected by Union
text:
## 1. Securities Transaction Tax (STT)
Item | Fact
Nature | Direct tax on buying and selling of securities on recognised stock exchanges
Law | Finance Act 2004; governed by the STT Act 2004; in force from 1 October 2004
Collection | At source by stock exchanges, mutual fund houses, IPO merchant bankers
Covers | Equity shares, futures and options, equity-oriented mutual funds
Exempt | Off-market deals, specific debt instruments, preference shares, government securities, bonds
Charged | Even on a loss; non-refundable
Aim: simplify capital gains taxation and curb its evasion
Commodities Transaction Tax (CTT): first proposed in Budget 2008-09, withdrawn; meant to put commodity futures on par with securities
⚠ States neither levy nor collect STT; it is a Union tax under List I

Statement | Status
Income from poultry farming, wool rearing in rural areas is exempt | Wrong: allied activities are not agricultural income

topic: Income tax, agricultural income and capital gains
t: Capital gains → when they arise
text:
## 1. Meaning
Capital gain = rise in value of a capital asset (property, shares, gold, painting), taxed when the asset is sold
Gain = selling price minus purchase price
Situation | Capital gain?
Natural increase in value of property owned | Yes
Painting bought, value rises with popularity | Yes
Increase in sales of a product | No: business income
Sale of inherited property | Yes (capital gains tax)
Inheriting property (no sale) | No: India has no inheritance tax
Income from inherited assets (interest, rent, dividends) is ordinary income
⚠ Rural agricultural land is not a capital asset, so no capital gain on it

text:
## 1. The definition UPSC tested
A foreign company transfers shares, and those shares derive substantial value from assets located in India
The sale happens outside India, between foreign entities, but India taxes it because the underlying value is Indian
Option in 2022 | Indirect transfer?
Indian company invests abroad, pays tax there | No
Foreign company invests in India, pays tax at home | No
Indian company buys assets abroad, sells at a gain | No
Foreign company transfers shares deriving value from Indian assets | Yes
## 2. Cases
Case | Fact
Vodafone-Hutchison | ~US$ 2.1 billion demand; SC ruled for Vodafone (2012); Finance Act 2012 taxed it retrospectively
Cairn | ~US$ 1.6 billion demand
Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 | Withdrew retrospective taxation of indirect transfers
PYQ 2022: answer (d); the other three options are direct cross-border investment

topic: Cross-border taxation: indirect transfers, equalisation levy
t: Equalisation levy → which law, what rate
text:
## 1. Features
Item | Fact
Law | Chapter VIII, Finance Act 2016, not the Income Tax Act
First levy | 6% on payments to non-residents for online advertisement services
2020 expansion | 2% on e-commerce supplies by non-residents
Nature | Direct tax on specified digital services (a "digital tax")
Aim | Level playing field between domestic and foreign digital firms
Not part of income tax, so it is outside DTAAs: non-residents cannot claim tax credit at home
⚠ Both 2018 statements were wrong: not under the Income Tax Act, and no DTAA credit
PYQ 2018: answer (d) neither 1 nor 2
## In news 2025-26
2% e-commerce levy abolished in August 2024
6% levy on online ads abolished from 1 April 2025

topic: Cross-border taxation: indirect transfers, equalisation levy
t: DTAA, TRC and GAAR → what each does
text:
## 1. Treaty terms
Term | Meaning
DTAA | Treaty so the same income is not taxed by both the source and the residence country
Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) | Certifies residence for a financial year; needed to claim DTAA benefits
Tax residency in India | Sec 6; generally a 182-day stay in a financial year
GAAR | Chapter X-A; denies tax benefit of an arrangement lacking commercial substance
GAAR applies only when the tax benefit exceeds ₹3 crore in a year; effective April 2017
Shaped by the Parthasarathi Shome Committee
⚠ GAAR can override DTAAs when an arrangement is mainly for tax avoidance
## In news 2025-26
Supreme Court (Jan 2026): Tiger Global's $1.6 billion Flipkart stake sale to Walmart (2018) is taxable in India; India-Mauritius DTAA benefit denied; a TRC alone is not enough

topic: Cross-border taxation: indirect transfers, equalisation levy

## 1. OECD two-pillar solution
Pillar | What it does
Pillar One | Reallocates part of large MNE profits to countries where their users/markets are
Pillar Two | Global minimum corporate tax of 15%

Income taken as a fixed % of turnover/receipts, no detailed books
Taxpayer | Presumed income
Small businesses (Sec 44AD) | 8% of turnover (6% for digital receipts)

topic: VAT and GST: design and institutions
t: VAT → features (and the one that is not)
text:
## 1. Features of Value Added Tax
Statement (2011) | True?
Multi-point, destination-based system of taxation | Yes
Levied on value addition at each stage of production-distribution | Yes
Tax on final consumption, ultimately borne by the consumer | Yes
Basically a Central subject, States only facilitators | No: VAT was a State subject (List II Entry 54)
State VAT was the precursor of GST; GST follows the same VAT method with input tax credit
⚠ VAT replaced State sales tax; States legislated, administered and collected it
PYQ 2011: odd one out is (d), the "Central subject" claim
## Beyond your notes
Haryana was first with VAT (April 2003); most States adopted it on 1 April 2005

topic: VAT and GST: design and institutions
t: GST → advantages (and what it does not do)
text:
## 1. What GST is
Comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax on every value addition; one indirect tax making India one common market
Destination-based: revenue goes to the State where goods are consumed
Rolled out 1 July 2017; Kelkar Task Force report led to the 2006 decision; "One Nation, One Tax"
Claimed advantage (2017) | Correct?
Replaces multiple taxes by multiple authorities → single market | Yes
Drastically cuts CAD, raises forex reserves | No: GST is a domestic tax
Makes India overtake China soon | No
## 2. Benefits in sources
Ends cascading (tax on tax) via input tax credit; better compliance; uniform structure, ease of business
NCERT: indirect tax reform aims at a common national market
PYQ 2017: answer 1 only

topic: VAT and GST: design and institutions
t: GST components → who levies on which supply
text:
## 1. Components
Component | Levied/collected by | Supply
CGST | Centre | Intra-state
SGST | State | Intra-state
UTGST | UT (without legislature) | Intra-UT
IGST | Centre (Art 269A), shared with destination State | Inter-state and imports
Intra-state sale: CGST + SGST together; inter-state sale: IGST only
Input Service Distributor (ISD): receives service invoices and distributes ITC to branches with the same PAN
ITC conditions: tax invoice from a registered dealer; used for business; not if depreciation claimed on the tax part
Implementing agency at Centre: CBIC; IT backbone: GSTN
⚠ IGST is levied by the Centre, not by the destination State; the State gets its share

Central taxes subsumed | State taxes subsumed
Central excise duty | State VAT/sales tax
Additional excise duties | Central Sales Tax
Excise under Medicinal and Toilet Preparations Act | Entry tax / octroi
Service tax | Luxury tax
Additional customs duty (CVD), SAD | Entertainment tax (not local bodies')

Alcoholic liquor for human consumption (constitutionally outside)
Five petroleum products: crude, petrol, diesel, natural gas, ATF (until the GST Council recommends)
Basic customs duty, stamp duty, electricity duty, property tax
"Declared goods of special importance" concept dropped

topic: VAT and GST: design and institutions

text:
## 1. Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016
Provision | Content
Art 246A | Concurrent power of Parliament and State legislatures to make GST laws; Parliament alone for inter-state supply
Art 269A | IGST on inter-state trade, levied and collected by the Centre, apportioned on Council advice
Art 279A | GST Council
Art 268A | Omitted (service tax)
GST compensation | Parliament to compensate States for 5 years
Bill passed August 2016; GST Council formed September 2016; GST from 1 July 2017

topic: VAT and GST: design and institutions
t: GST Council → composition and voting
text:
## 1. Structure
Item | Fact
Basis | Art 279A (constitutional body)
Chair | Union Finance Minister
Members | Union MoS Finance; Finance Ministers of all States and UTs with legislatures
Decision | Three-fourths of weighted votes of members present and voting
Weights | Centre one-third, all States together two-thirds
## 2. Recommends on
Taxes, cesses, surcharges to be subsumed; goods/services to be taxed or exempted
Model GST laws, apportionment of IGST, place of supply; rates including floor rates and bands
Special rate to raise resources during a natural calamity
Special provisions for North-East States, J&K, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand
Usually works by consensus; voting is rare
⚠ Neither side can pass a decision alone: the Centre (1/3) cannot reach 3/4 without States; States (2/3) cannot without the Centre
## Beyond your notes
Quorum: one-half of total members

t: Tax-to-GDP ratio falls → what it indicates
text:
## 1. The tested pair (2015)
Statement | UPSC key
Slowing economic growth rate | Correct (official key: answer a)
Less equitable distribution of national income | Wrong: the ratio does not measure distribution
Logic: when the economy slows, income, consumption and business activity fall, so tax collections fall relative to GDP

t: Tax-to-GDP ratio → meaning and India's figures
text:
## 1. Meaning
Total tax revenue ÷ nominal GDP, same year; key indicator of fiscal capacity
High ratio: formal economy, broad base; low ratio: informal sector, evasion
World Bank: 15% is the tipping point for sustainable growth and poverty reduction
## 2. India's figures
Measure | Value
Overall (Centre + States) | 19.6% (Bank of Baroda)
OECD average | 34%
Centre gross tax | 11.2% FY24, 11.7% FY25 projected (PMF)
Direct tax-to-GDP | 6.64% FY24, a 15-year high
States' own tax revenue | ~7% of GSDP
⚠ Preview (Budget 2026-27 data): Centre's gross tax-GDP 11.5% in 2024-25, 11.4% RE 2025-26, 11.2% BE 2026-27; PMF's figure differs
India is above Malaysia and Indonesia, below OECD and advanced economies

t: Tax buoyancy vs tax elasticity → meaning
text:
## 1. Buoyancy
% change in tax revenue ÷ % change in nominal GDP
Value | Meaning
Above 1 | Revenue grows faster than the economy
Below 1 | Revenue lags (evasion, exemptions, informality)
Sustained buoyancy above 1 raises the tax-to-GDP ratio
## 2. Figures
Long-term buoyancy 1.1 (PMF, 2025)
CBDT: buoyancy fell to 1.18 (2022-23) from 2.52 (2021-22)
CBDT data: Maharashtra gives the largest share of direct tax collections, then Delhi, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
## Beyond your notes
Tax elasticity measures response of revenue to GDP excluding discretionary changes (new rates, new taxes); buoyancy includes them
⚠ Buoyancy can exceed elasticity when rates are raised; elasticity reflects the tax system's built-in response

t: Tax terms → meaning
text:
## 1. Terms UPSC and State PSCs use
Term | Meaning
Tax expenditure | Revenue forgone through exemptions and incentives (not a waiver)
Laffer curve / Reaganomics | Lower rates can raise revenue by boosting growth (Arthur Laffer, 1970s; Reagan cuts 1980s)
Cascading | Tax on tax; removed by input tax credit
Inverted duty structure | Inputs taxed higher than the finished product
Black money | Income not declared for tax (Black Money Act 2015 for foreign assets)
Dabba trading | Illegal off-exchange trading that evades tax and SEBI oversight
PMF's "tax expenditure" line in one source reads "cost of collection as a share of tax"; the standard meaning is revenue forgone
## In news 2025-26
NUDGE approach of the Income Tax Department: ~25,000 taxpayers revised returns, foreign assets over ₹29,000 crore declared

text:

Tax | Key fact | Status

Inheritance/estate tax | On a deceased person's estate | Abolished 1985
Windfall gains tax | SAED on domestic crude and fuel exports after Russia-Ukraine price spike | Scrapped after ~30 months (Dec 2024)

Windfall tax was reviewed every two weeks; AED is also called the Road and Infrastructure Cess

t: Stamp duty and RoDTEP → who levies, what it refunds
text:
## 1. Stamp duty
Tax to register documents; stamped documents are valid evidence in court
Art 268 stamp duties: levied by the Centre, appropriated by the States
## 2. RoDTEP
Item | Fact
Launched | 2021, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
Replaced | MEIS (ruled an unlawful subsidy by a WTO panel)
Refunds | Hidden central, state, local duties on exports (VAT on fuel, electricity duty, mandi tax, stamp duty)
Form | Transferable e-scrips
