topic: Balance of payments: structure and classification
t: BoP → meaning, and why it beats the balance of trade
text:
## 1. Definition
Systematic record of all economic transactions between residents and the rest of the world in a period, normally a year
Not only goods, not only government-to-government, not only capital movements
## 2. BoT vs BoP
Point | Balance of Trade (BoT) | Balance of Payments (BoP)
Covers | Goods only (visibles) | Goods + services + income + transfers + capital
Place | Part of current account | Current + capital/financial accounts
Picture | Partial | Complete
Trade deficit = goods imports minus goods exports; CAD adds services, income, transfers
⚠ BoP is better because it includes visible and invisible items: A true, R true, R explains A
PYQ 2013: BoP = record of all transactions over a period (not just exports, not just govt deals)
PYQ 2006: Assertion-Reason on BoP vs BoT; answer (a)

topic: Balance of payments: structure and classification
t: Current account → what goes in it
text:
## 1. Components (CA Nov 2025, Testbook)
Head | Examples
Trade in goods (visibles) | Merchandise exports, imports
Services (invisibles) | IT, tourism, shipping, banking, insurance
Income (invisibles) | Interest, profit, dividends, wages
Current transfers (invisibles) | Private remittances, gifts, grants, pensions
Current account = balance of trade + balance of invisibles
Foreign tourist spending in India = export of services (forex inflow)
⚠ SDRs and foreign assets are NOT current account items (reserve / capital side)
⚠ India had a current account surplus in 2000-01 to 2002-03 (three years), a rarity (Testbook)
PYQ 2014: current account = 1 (BoT) + 3 (invisibles); PYQ 2011: Commonwealth Games visitors = export
## In news 2025-26
Services surplus record $188.8 bn in FY25, financing two-thirds of goods deficit (Economic Survey 2025-26)

topic: Balance of payments: structure and classification
t: Capital account → what goes in it
text:
## 1. Components
Item | Account
Foreign loans, ECBs, external assistance | Capital
FDI | Capital
Portfolio investment (FPI/FII) | Capital
NRI deposits, external bonds | Capital
Private remittances | Current (transfers)
IMF format: three parts: current + capital + financial account (APPSC); India often clubs capital and financial
Third block: errors and omissions and change in forex reserves
Testbook: no "deficit/surplus" concept used for the capital account in the same way as the current account
⚠ Remittances look like money flows but are current transfers
PYQ 2013: capital account = loans, FDI, portfolio (1, 2, 4); remittances excluded

topic: Balance of payments: structure and classification
t: Item → which account (the classification drill)
text:
## 1. Sort the item
Item | Account | Sub-head
Merchandise exports / imports, gold imports | Current | Trade (visible)
Foreign tourist spending in India | Current | Services export (invisible)
Indian students' fees abroad | Current | Services import
Shipping freight, insurance, software, royalties | Current | Services
Interest, dividends, profits paid or received | Current | Primary income
Private remittances, gifts, grants | Current | Secondary income / transfers
FDI, FPI, ADRs/GDRs | Capital / financial | Investment
ECBs, external assistance, trade credit | Capital / financial | Loans
NRI deposits (FCNR(B), NRE) | Capital / financial | Banking capital
Change in forex reserves, SDR holdings | Reserve account | Official reserves
⚠ Trap pairs: interest on a loan = current account, the loan itself = capital account; dividend = current, the FDI = capital
⚠ Remittances to India are not income earned in India: they are transfers
PYQ 2011 and 2014: tourist spending = export; SDRs and foreign assets are not current account items

topic: Balance of payments: structure and classification
t: BoP balance → autonomous vs accommodating, surplus vs deficit
text:
## 1. Two kinds of transactions (APPSC)
Type | Driven by | Position in BoP
Autonomous | Profit, trade motives, independent of BoP state | Above the line
Accommodating | The gap left by autonomous items | Below the line
Official reserve transactions (RBI selling or buying forex) are the accommodating item
BoP surplus = autonomous receipts > autonomous payments; deficit = the reverse
A CAD must be financed by a capital account surplus (net capital inflow) or by drawing down reserves
Capital account surplus = capital inflows (loans received, assets sold abroad) > outflows
Official reserve transactions matter more under fixed than under floating rates
## 2. Accounting identity
Current account + capital/financial account + errors and omissions + change in reserves = 0
So BoP always balances in accounting terms; "BoP deficit" means the overall balance before reserve use
⚠ "BoP is always in balance" (accounting) and "India had a BoP deficit" (overall balance) are both correct usages

topic: Balance of payments: structure and classification
t: India's BoP → the recent picture
text:
## 1. Structure of India's external account
Item | Usual sign | Note
Merchandise trade | Deficit | Oil, gold, electronics imports
Services | Surplus | Software, business services
Remittances | Surplus | World's largest recipient
Current account | Small deficit | Services + remittances offset goods gap
Capital account | Surplus | FDI, FPI, ECB, NRI deposits
Current account surplus years: 2000-01 to 2002-03 (Testbook)
Post-1991 pattern: capital surplus finances CAD; since mid-2024 capital inflows shrinking (PMF)
## In news 2025-26
CAD 0.8% of GDP in H1 FY26; services trade surplus offset goods deficit; remittances exceed gross FDI in most years (Economic Survey 2025-26)
FPI flows weak, driven by US rates ("flight to safety"); VRR and FAR routes steadied debt flows (Survey)
Outward FDI rose to $23.6 bn in FY25 (Singapore, US, UAE top destinations): ODI reduces net FDI
2026: Goldman Sachs cut India's CAD estimate to 1.1% of GDP, projected a BoP surplus of 0.7% of GDP (CA 360 June 2026); IMF: CAD may widen to $84.5 bn (~2%) in 2026 (PMF)
## Beyond your notes
India also ran a current account surplus in FY21 (~0.9% of GDP), a COVID-year import slump (verify)

topic: Forex reserves, import cover and liquidity
t: Forex reserves → the four components
text:
## 1. Components (PMF)
Component | Note
Foreign Currency Assets (FCA) | Largest, most liquid (USD, euro, pound, yen)
Gold | Last-resort asset, at market price
SDRs | IMF reserve asset, basket of 5 currencies
Reserve Tranche Position (RTP) | India's IMF quota-linked emergency line
Held by RBI, owned by the Government of India (CA Nov 2025)
SDR: created by IMF in 1969; basket = USD, euro, renminbi, yen, pound
⚠ Loans from the World Bank or foreign countries are NOT reserves
PYQ 2013: reserves = FCA + RBI gold + SDRs (options adding World Bank loans are traps)

topic: Forex reserves, import cover and liquidity
t: Import cover and reserve adequacy → what the indicators mean
text:
## 1. Indicators
Indicator | Meaning | Safer when
Import cover | Months of imports reserves can pay for | Higher
Short-term debt / reserves | Near-term repayment risk | Lower
Reserves / external debt | Debt cover | Higher
1991: reserves fell to barely two weeks of imports (NCERT)
⚠ Import cover is not imports/GDP, not annual import value, not export-import ratio
PYQ 2016: import cover = months of imports paid by international reserves
## In news 2025-26
$701.4 bn (16 Jan 2026): 11 months of imports, about 94% of external debt (Economic Survey 2025-26)
April 2026 (PMF): about $710 bn, 11-12 months cover, ~95% of external debt; $68 bn forward liabilities cut usable FCA below $500 bn
Sept 2026: RBI half-yearly report: $785.7 bn, India 4th globally, overtaking Russia (China, Japan, Switzerland ahead)
Survey: gold's share in reserves rose (diversification); RTP rose to $4.7 bn

topic: Forex reserves, import cover and liquidity
t: International liquidity → what the problem is
text:
## 1. Meaning
International liquidity = resources available to monetary authorities to finance BoP deficits
Components: gold, SDRs, foreign (hard) currencies
Hard currency: stable, globally accepted (US dollar, pound, euro)
Problem | Is it about?
Shortage of dollars and hard currencies | Yes
Shortage of goods and services | No
Shortage of gold and silver | No
Lack of exportable surplus | No
⚠ Today's link: reserves built on FPI inflows are weaker than those built on trade surpluses (CARE May 2026)
PYQ 2015: international liquidity = non-availability of dollars and other hard currencies

topic: Forex reserves, import cover and liquidity
t: SDR and reserve tranche → what they are, who issues them
text:
## 1. SDR (Special Drawing Right)
International reserve asset created by the IMF in 1969; allocated to members in proportion to quota
Not a currency; claim on freely usable currencies of members
Basket of 5: US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen, British pound
Used to support a member's BoP needs (Testbook)
## 2. Reserve Tranche Position (RTP)
Portion of India's IMF quota paid in reserve assets: drawable without conditions, an emergency credit line (PMF)
Point | SDR | Reserve tranche
Source | IMF allocation | India's own quota contribution
Conditions | None for use | None
India's value | Stable (Survey 2025-26) | Rose to $4.7 bn
## 3. IMF quotas
Quotas decide financial contribution, voting power, access to IMF resources; reviewed periodically (Testbook)
IMF and World Bank: Bretton Woods conference, 1944; India a founding member
⚠ World Bank loans and bilateral loans are not part of reserves; SDRs and RTP are
## Beyond your notes
SDR basket weights (2022 review): USD 43.38%, euro 29.31%, renminbi 12.28%, yen 7.59%, pound 7.44%; renminbi added in 2016 (as of 2026)

topic: Forex reserves, import cover and liquidity
t: Reserve adequacy → headline vs usable reserves
text:
## 1. Why reserves matter (PMF)
Role | How
Exchange management | RBI sells dollars in a managed float
Outflow cushion | Meets dollar demand during FPI exits
Import security | Pays for crude, fertiliser, machinery
Credibility | Lowers sovereign borrowing costs
## 2. Concerns
Net reality: $68 bn forward liabilities cut usable FCA below headline (PMF Apr 2026)
Flow dependence: reserves built on volatile capital inflows, not trade surpluses
Metric gap: import cover and short-term debt ratios ignore portfolio equity outflows
Dollar sales drain rupee liquidity; RBI offsets via open market operations
⚠ Reserves fell by $51.52 bn in three months of intervention (PMF Feb 2025); and by ~$30 bn in early 2026
Likely next: "Forex reserves include forward contracts" (no; forward liabilities reduce usable reserves)

topic: Convertibility, Tarapore and the forex regime
t: Convertibility → current vs capital account
text:
## 1. Meaning
Convertibility = freely converting rupee into foreign currency and vice versa at a market rate
Type | For what | India
Current account convertibility | Trade in goods, services, income, transfers | Full since 19-20 Aug 1994
Capital account convertibility | Trading financial assets (FDI, portfolio, loans) | Partial
1994: India accepted IMF Article VIII (no curbs on current transactions)
⚠ Rupee is not convertible into gold; convertibility is not "value fixed by market forces"
⚠ Only current account is fully convertible: options with capital account or gold are wrong
PYQ 2015: convertibility = conversion to other currencies and back; PYQ 2000: fully convertible on current account only
PYQ 1998: capital account convertibility = exchange for trading financial assets

topic: Convertibility, Tarapore and the forex regime
t: Path to convertibility → years and steps
text:
## 1. Timeline
Year | Step
1991 | Devaluation in two steps (1 and 3 July)
March 1992 | LERMS: dual rate, 60% market, 40% official
March 1993 | Unified market-determined rate; trade fully convertible
March 1994 | Invisibles and remittances freely convertible
Aug 1994 | Article VIII: full current account convertibility
May 1997 | Tarapore Committee I report (RBI) on capital account convertibility
Sept 2006 | Tarapore Committee II: fuller capital account convertibility
⚠ Testbook dates LERMS to Budget 1992-93, fully operational March 1993; Preview says partial convertibility from March 1992: same reform
⚠ Tarapore = capital account convertibility, not SEZs, forex reserves or oil prices
PYQ 2007: Tarapore Committee = fuller capital account convertibility

topic: Convertibility, Tarapore and the forex regime

text:
## 1. Liberalised Remittance Scheme (PMF Prelims Magnum 2025)
Point | Rule
Limit | USD 2,50,000 per financial year (April-March)
Who | Resident individuals, including minors (guardian countersigns)
Not allowed | Corporates, partnership firms, HUFs, trusts
Frequency | No limit on number of remittances
Currency | Any freely convertible foreign currency
Use | Permissible current or capital account transactions, or both
Needs Indian bank account, PAN, passport
Current uses: travel (except Nepal and Bhutan), gifts, donations, studies, employment, emigration
2025: residents can open foreign currency accounts / dollar FDs in GIFT City IFSC under LRS

## Beyond your notes
Corporate overseas direct investment up to $500 mn a year without approval (Testbook figure; verify current ODI rules)

topic: Convertibility, Tarapore and the forex regime
t: ECB → what it is and the 2026 rules
text:
## 1. Meaning (PMF LENS Feb 2026)
Commercial loans raised by eligible resident entities from recognised non-residents
Governed by RBI under FEMA 1999; in any freely convertible currency or in rupees
Two routes: Automatic (no RBI approval) and Approval route
## 2. Key changes in the revised framework
Item | Old | New
Automatic limit | $750 mn a year | $1 bn or 300% of net worth
Cost | All-in-cost ceiling | Market-determined rates
Maturity | Tiered | Unified minimum average maturity 3 years
Manufacturers |  | Up to $150 mn at 1-3 years
Eligible borrowers | Listed types | Any entity under a Central/State Act
RBI-regulated entities may on-lend ECB proceeds to individuals (not real estate); proceeds may fund acquisitions
⚠ Easing ECB rules = a rupee-defence measure (more dollar inflow), PYQ 2019
⚠ Unhedged ECBs hurt when the rupee falls: 5% depreciation raises servicing cost 5% (PMF)

topic: Convertibility, Tarapore and the forex regime
t: Rupee internationalisation → tools and limits
text:
## 1. Meaning
Allowing the INR to be used outside India for trade, investment and financial transactions
## 2. Tools (PMF)
Tool | What it is
Special Rupee Vostro Accounts (SRVA) | Foreign bank's rupee account with an Indian bank, for trade settlement in INR
Currency swap agreements | SAARC, UAE, BRICS
Masala bonds | Rupee bonds issued abroad
Rupee trade | Nepal, Bhutan, Iran, etc.
Non-resident rupee accounts | Foundation for wider use
Vostro = "your account with us" (foreign bank's account held by Indian bank); Nostro = "our account with you"
Nov 2025: SRVA surplus balances can be invested in corporate bonds and commercial papers (PMF)
Gains: needs fewer forex reserves, cuts dollar dependence; risk: early volatility, outflows
⚠ Barrier: INR not fully convertible on capital account; full internationalisation needs it
Likely next: Statement-I/II on Vostro accounts and rupee trade as a way to reduce dollar demand

topic: Convertibility, Tarapore and the forex regime

text:
## Beyond your notes
Law | Year | Nature
FERA | 1973 | Criminal, control-oriented
FEMA | 1999 (in force June 2000) | Civil, management-oriented
PMLA | 2002 | Money laundering (criminal)
Enforcement Directorate enforces FEMA and PMLA

Hawala transactions breach FEMA and PMLA

topic: Convertibility, Tarapore and the forex regime
t: Hawala → what it is
text:
## 1. Meaning (PMF LENS)
Informal transfer outside official banking channels; no physical movement of money
Runs on trust through brokers called hawaladars; settlement later via cash, property, services
Point | Fact
Origin | South Asia, about 8th century
Users | Migrant workers, traders evading controls
Risk | Terror financing, money laundering
⚠ Hawala = rupee payment against foreign currency (and back) without official channels, not share sales or party funding
PYQ 1996: hawala relates to rupees against overseas currencies outside official channels
## In news 2025-26
2025: SC said Bitcoin trading resembles a refined form of hawala (LENS May 2025)

topic: Exchange rate: regimes, devaluation, NEER-REER, PPP
t: Exchange rate regimes → fixed, floating, managed float
text:
## 1. Types (PMF)
Regime | How rate is set
Fixed | Central bank uses reserves to hold a rate
Floating | Market forces, no intervention
Managed float | Market rate + RBI intervention
India: managed float since the 2010s; RBI curbs volatility, does not target a level
PMF: 2022-24 RBI ran a near-fixed approach; IMF reclassified India from floating to "stabilised arrangement" (Dec 2022-Oct 2023)
Impossible trinity (Mundell-Fleming): fixed rate, free capital, independent monetary policy: pick two
Dornbusch overshooting: rate over-depreciates short run as goods prices are sticky
⚠ Currency price is set by demand for the country's goods/services and govt stability, not the World Bank
PYQ 2012: answer = 2 and 3 (demand, stability); economic potential not in the key

topic: Exchange rate: regimes, devaluation, NEER-REER, PPP
t: Nominal vs real exchange rate → definitions
text:
## 1. Terms (PMF LENS Jan 2025)
Term | Meaning
Nominal exchange rate | Price of foreign currency in domestic currency (₹ per $)
Real exchange rate | Relative price of foreign goods vs domestic goods (adjusts for prices)
Effective exchange rate (EER) | Rate against a trade-weighted basket; weights = partner's share in India's trade
A lower real exchange rate (in the competitiveness sense) improves export competitiveness
Nominal depreciation helps exports only if the real rate also depreciates
India's higher inflation means a stronger real rate despite nominal depreciation: export gain cancelled
⚠ Rupee: ₹45.56/$ (2010-11) → ₹86.95/$ (Feb 2025): steady weakening despite RBI action
⚠ "₹ per $ rising" = depreciation; do not read a higher number as a stronger rupee

topic: Exchange rate: regimes, devaluation, NEER-REER, PPP
t: Regime history → Bretton Woods to managed float
text:
## 1. Global (Testbook)
Phase | Rule
Bretton Woods (1944) | Currencies pegged to US dollar; dollar pegged to gold
Aim | Stop competitive devaluations of the Great Depression era
End | Abandoned in the early 1970s
After | Floating and managed floats
## 2. India
Year | Regime
1991 | Devaluation; start of freeing the rate
1992 | LERMS dual rate
1993 | Market-determined unified rate
2010s | Managed float (RBI curbs volatility)
2022-24 | Near-fixed; IMF tag "stabilised arrangement"
## Beyond your notes
Rupee was linked to the pound sterling until 1971 and to a basket of currencies from 1975
US ended dollar-gold convertibility in 1971 (Nixon shock)

topic: Exchange rate: regimes, devaluation, NEER-REER, PPP
t: Rupee depreciation → who gains, who loses
text:
## 1. Winners and losers (PMF)
Gains | Loses
Exporters: IT, pharma, textiles, autos | Importers: oil and gas, electronics
IT margins: +20-30 bps per 1% fall | Firms with unhedged ECBs
NRI remittances (more rupees per dollar) | Students and travellers abroad
FDI (Indian assets cheaper in $) | Consumers (imported inflation)
Oil and input-import dependence limits the export gain (PMF)
## In news 2025-26
Rupee fell 5.4% vs USD in FY26 (to Jan), among the most depreciated with the yen (Economic Survey)
Record trade deficit $41.7 bn (Oct 2025); FDI inflows up 14% to $81.04 bn (PMF)
Survey: long-run currency strength comes from savings-investment balance and manufacturing exports, not financial openness alone
⚠ Wider trade deficits need not cause depreciation if net foreign investment covers them (Survey)

topic: Exchange rate: regimes, devaluation, NEER-REER, PPP
t: Devaluation vs depreciation → effects UPSC tests
text:
## 1. Terms
Term | Meaning
Devaluation | Official cut in value under a fixed rate
Depreciation | Market-driven fall (₹60 → ₹65 per $)
Appreciation | Fewer rupees per dollar
## 2. Effects of devaluation
Statement | Verdict
Makes exports more competitive | Necessarily true
Raises foreign value of currency | False (lowers it)
Improves trade balance | Not necessarily
India: devaluations in 1949, 1966, 1991 (1991 in two steps, ~18-19%); Testbook gives 1991 as 22% (₹21 → ₹27)
⚠ India's import-heavy exports and oil dependence blunt the gain (PMF, CARE May 2026)
PYQ 2021: only 1 correct; PYQ 1999: devaluation may promote exports as prices fall abroad: A, R true, R explains A

topic: Exchange rate: regimes, devaluation, NEER-REER, PPP
t: NEER and REER → what a rise means
text:
## 1. Definitions (PMF)
Point | NEER | REER
Measures | Rupee vs trade-weighted basket | NEER adjusted for inflation differentials
Rise means | Rupee appreciation | Loss of competitiveness
RBI NEER baskets: 6 currencies (USD, euro, yuan, pound, yen, HK dollar) and 40 currencies (~88% of trade); base 2015-16 = 100
Higher domestic inflation than partners widens the NEER-REER gap (REER rises above NEER)
⚠ A rising REER is not an improvement: exports dearer, imports cheaper
PYQ 2022: statements 1 and 3 correct, 2 wrong
## In news 2025-26
REER index hit a record 108.14 (PMF 2025)
Rupee: ₹86.95/$ (Feb 2025), new low near ₹90 (PMF 2026); ₹93/$ on 17 April 2026 (Preview)

topic: Exchange rate: regimes, devaluation, NEER-REER, PPP
t: PPP → method and India's rank
text:
## 1. Method
PPP exchange rate: compare prices of the same basket of goods and services across countries
Corrects for cost-of-living gaps; used for HDI income, World Bank poverty line ($3/day, PPP 2021)
Measure | India's rank
PPP GDP | 3rd (after China, US)
Nominal GDP (2024) | 5th (after US, China, Germany, Japan)
⚠ India is 3rd, not 6th in PPP terms
PYQ 2019: statement 1 correct, 2 wrong
## In news 2025-26
EY report (Sept 2025): India may be 2nd-largest PPP economy by 2038 ($34.2 trn); $20.7 trn PPP by 2030

topic: CAD, currency crisis and defending the rupee
t: Reducing CAD → which actions help
text:
## 1. Actions
Action | Effect on CAD
Devaluing the currency | Reduces (exports up, imports dearer)
Attracting FDI and FII funds | Helps finance/reduce CAD
Cutting export subsidy | Worsens (exports fall)
Import substitution, higher import tariffs | Helps
Higher export duties | Does not help
CAD = imports of goods, services, transfers exceed exports
Post-1991, capital account surpluses financed CADs; since mid-2024 shrinking inflows (PMF)
⚠ FDI/FII is a capital account item, yet Preview counts it as easing CAD over time
PYQ 2011: answer 1 and 3
## In news 2025-26
CAD 0.8% of GDP (H1 FY26) (Economic Survey); IMF projects $84.5 bn (~2% of GDP) in 2026 (PMF)
Record goods trade deficit ~$41.7-42 bn (Oct 2025): US tariffs, gold imports

topic: CAD, currency crisis and defending the rupee
t: Currency crisis → what lowers the risk
text:
## 1. Meaning
Sudden, sharp depreciation, often from massive capital flight (PMF)
Factor | Effect on crisis risk
IT services forex earnings | Reduces
Remittances | Reduces (no repayment burden, counter-cyclical)
Higher govt expenditure | Does not reduce
High CAD, volatile FPI, inflation gap | Raises
2013 taper tantrum: India in Morgan Stanley's "Fragile Five"
PYQ 2019: answer 1 and 3
## In news 2025-26
India largest remittance recipient: $135.4 bn in FY25 (Economic Survey; PMF: $135.46 bn)
! PMF LENS (June 2026) cites a separate series: workers' remittances record $110.47 bn in FY26 (from $87.55 bn)
May 2026: PM urged cutting import-linked consumption amid the Iran conflict; BoP as weak as 2013 (PMF)

topic: CAD, currency crisis and defending the rupee
t: Stopping the rupee slide → measures used and not used
text:
## 1. Measures (PMF 2026)
Measure | Used?
RBI sells dollars (spot, forward) | Yes
Monetary tightening (higher rates) | Yes
Curb non-essential imports (gold duty), push exports | Yes
Encourage Masala bonds; ease ECB rules; FCNR(B) incentives | Yes
Special Vostro rupee trade settlement | Yes
Curbs on banks in offshore NDF market | Yes
Expansionary monetary policy | No: weakens rupee
Masala bond: rupee-denominated bond abroad; investor bears currency risk; first by IFC (Nov 2014)
⚠ Expansionary policy lowers rates, triggers capital flight and inflation
PYQ 2019: the measure NOT used = expansionary monetary policy
## In news 2025-26
RBI net-sold ~$20.1 bn spot (Jan-Sep 2025); export realisation window 9 → 15 months (Nov 2025)
2026: RBI FCNR(B), ECB and OFCB swap facility; minimum 3-year tenor (LENS June 2026)

topic: CAD, currency crisis and defending the rupee
t: RBI's forex toolkit → swaps, NDF curbs, FCNR(B)
text:
## 1. Instruments (PMF LENS 2026)
Tool | What it is
Forex swap | Exchange currencies now at spot, reverse later at a set rate
FCNR(B) deposit | NRI fixed deposit in foreign currency (USD, pound, euro, yen, CAD, AUD) with Indian banks
Non-Deliverable Forward/Derivative (NDF/NDD) | Rate agreed, no currency delivered, cash-settled (usually USD); traded offshore (Singapore, London)
Spot / forward sales | RBI sells dollars to meet demand
## 2. 2026 measures
Swap window covers FCNR(B) deposits (min 3-year tenor), ECBs (avg maturity ≥3 years, swap up to 5 years) and banks' OFCBs; covers principal only
Banks may lend to non-residents against FCNR(B) deposits
April 2026: RBI banned banks from NDD contracts to curb rupee volatility and speculation
⚠ FCNR(B): exchange risk on the bank, not the NRI; interest tax-free, fully repatriable
⚠ NDFs are offshore and cash-settled: they move the onshore rupee without any rupee changing hands

topic: CAD, currency crisis and defending the rupee
t: 1991 BoP crisis → causes and response
text:
## 1. Causes (NCERT)
Fiscal profligacy of the 1980s: spending far above revenue
Imports rising fast without matching exports; forex borrowed abroad spent on consumption
Reserves fell to barely two weeks (a fortnight) of imports; could not pay interest to lenders
Rising prices of essentials
## 2. Response
Step | Detail
Loan | $7 bn from IBRD (World Bank) and IMF
Conditions | Liberalise, reduce govt role, remove trade curbs
New Economic Policy | Stabilisation (short-term: BoP, inflation) + structural reforms (long-term: LPG)
Rupee | Devalued (July 1991): forex inflow rose, path to market rate
⚠ Stabilisation = short-term; structural reform = long-term: a favourite swap trap
PYQ link: 1991 devaluation + 1994 current account convertibility = the "path" questions (2000, 1999)
## Beyond your notes
Gulf War (1990-91) oil spike and NRI deposit outflows triggered the crisis; India pledged gold with the Bank of England and Bank of Japan

t: India's external debt → who owes it, in which currency
text:
## 1. Composition (end-Dec 2025, Preview)
Item | Value / share
Total | $765.5 bn
Non-government | $596.8 bn (most)
Government (sovereign) | $168.7 bn
US dollar | 54.8%
Indian rupee | 30.1%
Yen / SDR / Euro | 6.3% / 4.3% / 3.7%
Largest components: commercial borrowings, then NRI deposits, short-term trade credit
States cannot contract external debt; the Centre borrows and on-lends (APPSC)
⚠ Neither "mostly government" nor "all in dollars" is true
PYQ 2019: neither statement correct
## In news 2025-26
Economic Survey: $718.2 bn (end-Dec 2024), 18.4% of GDP; India 21st globally, 11th in G20; NIIP -8.7% of GDP

t: External debt and IIP → the ratios to know
text:
## 1. Indicators (Economic Survey 2025-26)
Indicator | India
External debt | $718.2 bn (end-Dec 2024), +10.7% YoY
Debt-to-GDP | 18.4%: among least leveraged EMs
Share in GoI's total debt | Less than 5%
Forex reserves / external debt | ~94%
Net IIP | -$0.3 trn; -8.7% of GDP (from -10.1%, and -14.1% five years ago)
Assets-to-liabilities ratio | 77.5%
IIP = stock of a country's external financial assets minus liabilities; negative = net debtor
India = 11th largest debtor (net IIP); Germany overtook Japan as largest creditor (2024)
Advanced economies hold 88.1% of global external debt
Debt trap: new loans taken just to pay interest on old loans (Preview)
⚠ Major component of India's external debt = commercial borrowings (Preview: still true since 2017), not short-term debt
⚠ Preview end-Dec 2025 figure ($765.5 bn) is later than the Survey's end-Dec 2024 figure: both can appear

t: Immunity to a global crisis → what protects India
text:
## 1. Policies
Policy | Gives immunity?
Not depending on short-term foreign borrowing | Yes
Opening to more foreign banks | No: raises exposure
Full capital account convertibility | No: flows can reverse
Short-term debt must be repaid fast; a crisis turns it into capital flight
1997 East Asian crisis: prolonged over-valuation of currencies; began in Thailand (July 1997)
1991 crisis: India got $7 bn from World Bank and IMF; stabilisation + structural reforms (NCERT)
⚠ Tarapore-style full CAC is a risk, not a shield
PYQ 2020: only 1 gives immunity
## Beyond your notes
In 1991 India pledged gold (shipped to the Bank of England) to raise funds

t: FDI definition → the 10% line
text:
## 1. Legal definition (FEMA NDI Rules 2019)
FDI = investment through capital instruments by a person resident outside India
Company type | Counts as FDI when foreign stake is
Unlisted Indian company | Any stake
Listed Indian company | 10% or more of post-issue paid-up equity, fully diluted basis
Below 10% in a listed company = FPI (portfolio)
Aim: lasting interest and control; investor joins day-to-day management
## 2. Rule book
FEMA 1999 → FEMA (Non-Debt Instruments) Rules 2019 + Consolidated FDI Policy 2020
DPIIT (Commerce Ministry) frames FDI policy; RBI enforces reporting and compliance
⚠ Unlisted company: any foreign equity is FDI; the 10% test is only for listed firms
⚠ FDI is not "essentially in a listed company" (PYQ 2020 option a was the trap)

t: Instruments → FDI or not
text:
## 1. Classification (PYQ 2021 list and its neighbours)
Instrument | FDI? | Why
FCCB (foreign currency convertible bond) | Yes | Convertible into equity
GDR / ADR (depository receipts) | Yes | Issued against Indian shares
FII/FPI investment with conditions (10%+, convertible) | Yes | Reclassified as FDI
Equity, compulsorily convertible debentures and preference shares, share warrants | Yes | Capital instruments
NRE deposits (non-resident external) | No | Debt-creating bank deposits
Portfolio investment (<10%) | No | FPI
ECB (external commercial borrowing) | No | Loan = debt
Government securities | No | Debt; FDI is not in G-secs
⚠ PYQ 2021 answer: 1, 2 and 3 (FCCB, FII with conditions, GDR); NRE deposits out
PYQ 2021: "which can be included in FDI"; trap: NRE deposits look like foreign money but are debt

t: FDI as a capital flow → non-debt creating
text:
## 1. Character of FDI
Feature | FDI | Loan / ECB
Creates debt? | No (equity) | Yes
Debt servicing (interest + principal) | None | Required
Return to investor | Dividends, profits | Interest
Stability | Long-term, sticky | Fixed tenure
FDI = largely non-debt-creating capital flow (PYQ 2020 correct option)
Brings capital + technology + management skills, competition, jobs, export competitiveness
## 2. PYQ 2020 options decoded
a) "Essentially in a listed company" → wrong (unlisted counts too)
b) "Largely non-debt creating" → correct
c) "Involves debt-servicing" → wrong
d) "By FIIs in Government securities" → wrong (that is FPI debt)
PYQ 2020: core feature of FDI; trap: options mixing FDI with FPI and ECB features

t: Forms of FDI → what qualifies as direct investment
text:
## 1. Included in FDI (PYQ 2012)
Form | FDI?
Subsidiaries of foreign companies in India | Yes
Majority foreign equity in Indian companies | Yes
Companies exclusively financed by foreign companies | Yes
Joint ventures with foreign partner | Yes
Portfolio investment | No
PYQ 2012 answer: 1, 2 and 3 only
## 2. Types by mode and direction
Type | Meaning | Example
Greenfield | New facility from scratch | Hyundai plant, Sriperumbudur (TN)
Brownfield | Acquire or merge existing firm | Vodafone buying Hutchison Essar
Horizontal | Same business abroad | Market reach
Vertical | Backward/forward stage of supply chain | Control inputs
Conglomerate | Unrelated industry abroad | Diversification

t: Gross FDI, net FDI and outward FDI → what each means
text:
## 1. Formula
Net FDI = Gross FDI inflows − (Repatriation by foreign firms + Outward FDI by Indian firms)
OFDI/ODI = Indian firms investing abroad; reduces net FDI but internationalises Indian firms
Measure | 2024-25 | 2025-26
Gross inflows | $81 bn (+14%) | Record $94.53 bn (earlier peak $84.84 bn, 2021-22)
Repatriation | high | $53.58 bn
Outward FDI | $23.6 bn (+75%) | $33.29 bn
Net FDI | crashed >96%, near zero | $7.65 bn
Gross foreign inflow-to-GDP: 3.1% (2020-21) → 2.1% (2024-25); net FDI 1.6% → ~0%
OFDI top destinations: Singapore, US, UAE (also Mauritius, Netherlands)
⚠ Net FDI falls when repatriation (IPO exits, profit booking) and OFDI rise, even if gross inflow is a record
## In news 2025-26
Economic Survey 2025-26: India's average return on inward FDI ~7.3%; risk-adjusted return 2nd only to Indonesia
⚠ FY26 gross FDI: LENS (Oct 2026) gives $94.53 bn; LENS (May 2026) gives $90 bn; follow PMF's latest, $94.53 bn

t: FDI vs FPI/FII → the key differences
text:
## 1. Comparison
Feature | FDI | FPI / FII
Stake | 10%+ listed / any unlisted | <10% listed
Control | Management control | No control
Horizon | Long-term, strategic | Short-term, speculative
Volatility | Stable | Volatile ("hot money")
Target | Specific sectors/enterprises | General capital via stock and bond markets
Brings | Capital + technology + management | Financial capital only
Market | Primary assets, plants | Mostly secondary market
Entry barriers | Higher (approvals, caps) | Lower
PYQ 2011 answer: FII increases capital availability in general; FDI targets specific sectors
⚠ Traps in 2011 options: FII does not bring management skills; FII is less stable; FDI does not flow only into the secondary market
PYQ 2011: "best represents an important difference"; trap: swapping FDI and FII features

t: FPI regulation → categories, limits, routes
text:
## 1. Basics
Capital market opened to FPI/FII in 1994; regulator SEBI; foreign investment ceilings maintained by RBI
FII + QFI merged into single FPI regime (SEBI FPI Regulations 2014, now 2019)
SEBI FPI category (Testbook) | Who
Category I | Government and government-related bodies, central banks
Category II | Regulated funds, mutual funds, banks
Category III | Others
## 2. Limits and debt routes
Item | Rule
Single FPI in one company | <10% of paid-up equity (fully diluted)
Breach of 10% | Sell surplus or reclassify as FDI within 5 trading days
Corporate bonds | 15% of outstanding stock (raised from 9% in Budget 2020-21)
G-secs / SDLs | 6% / 2%
VRR (Voluntary Retention Route) | Keep 75% invested for minimum 3 years
FAR (Fully Accessible Route) | No caps in designated G-secs for FPIs, NRIs, OCIs
⚠ Reclassification to FDI is not allowed in sectors prohibited for FDI; needs investee company concurrence and land-border approvals

t: Participatory Notes and FPI instruments → what they are
text:
## 1. P-Notes
Participatory Note (PN) = Offshore Derivative Instrument with Indian stocks as underlying
Issued by SEBI-registered FPIs to overseas investors who do not register with SEBI
Started 2000; criticised for anonymity and round-tripping
PYQ 2007 and 2019: P-Notes linked to FIIs/FPIs (not CDs, CPs or promissory notes)
## 2. Who is who
Term | Meaning
FII | Older label for foreign institutional investor (pension funds, mutual funds, hedge funds)
FPI | Current umbrella regime for portfolio investors
FVCI | Foreign venture capital investor
ECB | Overseas loan to Indian firm (debt)
DII | Domestic institutional investors: mutual funds, insurers

t: FPI flows and reforms → 2025-26 developments
text:
## In news 2025-26
FPIs were net sellers April-December 2025 (high US yields, rupee fall, tariff uncertainty)
DIIs' share (18.3%) overtook FIIs' (16.7%, a 13-year low) in NSE-listed equity value (Sept 2025)
SEBI SWAGAT-FI/"SWAFAT-FI" single window for trusted FPIs (sovereign funds, regulated retail funds); India Market Access Portal

topic: FDI policy: routes, caps and bans
t: Automatic vs government route → what each needs
text:
## 1. Two routes
Route | Approval | Reporting
Automatic | No prior approval of Government or RBI | Post-facto report to RBI
Government | Prior approval via Foreign Investment Facilitation Portal (FIFP) by administrative ministry | Same
Government route for sensitive sectors: defence (beyond cap), multi-brand retail, broadcasting, print media
## 2. Approving authority (history)
FIPB (Foreign Investment Promotion Board): moved to Finance Ministry (DEA) in 2003; abolished 2017
Now: administrative ministries approve, DPIIT is nodal; ministries cannot reject without DPIIT concurrence (2026 SOP)
Large proposals (above ₹5,000 crore equity rise with changed ownership): CCEA
⚠ FIPB no longer exists; questions saying "FIPB approves" are outdated

topic: FDI policy: routes, caps and bans
t: Four categories of FDI → route and cap
text:
## 1. PMF classification

## 1. Comparison
Feature | Customs port | Transhipment port
Purpose | Manages national EXIM trade | Transfers cargo ship to ship for other destinations

Revenue | Duties, warehousing, EXIM handling | Vessel and container services

About 75% of India's transhipment cargo was handled at Colombo, Singapore, Klang (and Jebel Ali)

Refining, processing, storage, transportation, distribution, marketing and sale of petroleum, petroleum products and natural gas

Venture capital (VC) = long-term start-up capital for new entrepreneurs with high growth potential
A form of private equity; comes from investors, investment banks, financial institutions; usually for equity stake

Short-term capital to industries | No | Working capital

No statutory backing, no law mandating enforcement; private traders not bound
Uniform for the whole country; a floor, not a ceiling

Procurement at MSP is unlimited for all cereals, pulses, oilseeds in every State | False

MSP is legally enforceable against private buyers | False
Procurement is mostly rice, wheat, limited pulses, a few States | True

A2+FL | A2 + imputed value of family labour

## 1. Sugar MSP (not to confuse with crop MSP)
Minimum Selling Price of sugar = minimum ex-mill price below which mills cannot sell sugar in the domestic market

Reserve of foodgrains (mainly wheat, rice) to stabilise prices and ensure food security; introduced in Fourth Plan (1969-74)

t: Agricultural markets → which law regulates them
text:
## 1. APMC = State law
Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) = statutory body set up by state governments under their own State APMC Acts
Agricultural marketing is a State subject: intra-state trade → states; inter-state trade → Centre
Some commodities (raw jute, cotton) are regulated by both state and central authorities
Law | What it does | Regulates mandis?
State APMC Acts | Notified produce; first sale in APMC yard via licensed agents | Yes
Essential Commodities Act, 1955 | Centre (and states) control production, supply, distribution, stock limits, prices of notified goods (also drugs, fertilisers, textiles, coal) | No
Agricultural Produce (Grading and Marking) Act, 1937 | First central law on grading standards (AGMARK) | No
Fruit Products Order 1955 / Meat Food Products Order 1973 | Food quality orders | No
⚠ The EC Act's scope is broader than the APMC Act, but it does not regulate agricultural markets

topic: Agricultural marketing: APMC system and reforms
t: APMC mandis → functions and problems
text:
## 1. How the mandi system works
Farmers sell in regulated market yards by open auction or e-bidding; first sale of notified produce must be inside the APMC area through licensed commission agents
~2,477 principal regulated markets + 4,843 sub-market yards (Testbook)
Mandi density: 1 per 450 sq km vs recommended 80 sq km (PMF)
## 2. Objectives vs problems
APMC objectives | Problems flagged
Price transparency, fair dealing | Licensed traders' monopoly, cartelisation → monopsony
Same-day payment to farmers | Multiple licences to trade across market areas
Market-led extension, publish arrivals/prices | High levies: market fee, mandi tax, commission, VAT
PPP in market management | APMC fees not under legislative oversight; politically controlled boards
Farmers' share only 30-40% for perishables; post-harvest losses 20-30% (PMF)
## In news 2025-26
Haryana introduced Aadhaar-based biometric verification of farmers at mandis before procurement (LENS Apr 2026) to stop crops from other states being sold under local identities

topic: Agricultural marketing: APMC system and reforms
t: Model Acts on marketing → key provisions
text:
## 1. Model APMC Act, 2003 (Testbook)
Private markets by individuals, farmers, consumers in any area
Direct sale to contract-farming sponsors; special markets for perishables
Consumers' and farmers' markets; single market fee; registration instead of licensing of functionaries
APMC revenue to be used for market infrastructure; Karnataka model cited as successful
## 2. Model contract farming law, 2018
Model Agricultural Produce and Livestock Contract Farming and Services (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, 2018: contract farming kept outside APMC Act
No title/right in land vests in sponsor; no permanent structures on farmer's land; sponsor must buy entire pre-agreed quantity; FPOs can contract; registration with RARC; contracted produce insurable
## Beyond your notes
Model APLM Act, 2017 (Agricultural Produce and Livestock Marketing (Promotion and Facilitation) Act): whole state one market area; livestock included; private market yards, direct marketing, farmer-consumer markets; warehouses/silos/cold stores declared market sub-yards; caps on market fee (about 1% fruits and vegetables, 2% foodgrains) and commission (verify)
⚠ Model Acts are advisory: states must adopt them; the Centre cannot impose them (marketing is a State subject)

## 1. The three Farm Acts (Sept 2020, repealed 1 Dec 2021)
Act | Core provision
Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act | Trade outside APMC yards; states barred from levying fee/cess outside APMC areas
Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act | Contract farming
Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act | Removed stock limits except in extraordinary price rise
⚠ The Trade Act did not mention MSP, EC or contract farming; each was in a different Act
## 2. Farmer-to-consumer channels (NCERT)
Channel | State
Apni Mandi | Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan
Hadaspar Mandi | Pune (Maharashtra)
Rythu Bazars | Andhra Pradesh (fruits, vegetables)
Uzhavar Sandies | Tamil Nadu

t: e-NAM → features and objective
text:
## 1. National Agriculture Market (e-NAM)
Pan-India electronic trading portal linking existing APMC mandis into a unified national market
Launched 14 April 2016; Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare
Lead agency: Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC)

t: State → its four elements
text:
## 1. Definition UPSC accepted (2021)
Garner: State is "a community of persons, more or less numerous, permanently occupying a definite territory, independent (or nearly so) of external control, and possessing an organised government to which the great body of inhabitants render habitual obedience"
Bluntschli: "the politically organised people of a definite territory"
Element | Meaning
People / Population | Community of persons permanently living there (no minimum size)
Territory | Demarcated boundary separating one State from another; includes airspace, territorial sea, sub-soil
Government | Organised machinery that makes, enforces, adjudicates law
Sovereignty | Independent say in all domestic and external decisions; most important element
⚠ India before 1947 was not a State: it had people, territory and government but no sovereignty (British control)
⚠ Trap options of 2021: "culture, tradition" (that is a nation), "executive responsible + independent judiciary" (that is a form of government), "protect natural rights" (a purpose, not an element)
PYQ 2021: "best defines the term State" → community + definite territory + independent of external control + organised government

t: State vs government, nation and society
text:
## 1. Terms UPSC options mix up
Term | What it is | Key difference
State | People + territory + government + sovereignty | Permanent; abstract; only it is sovereign
Government | Agency through which the State acts | Temporary, changes at elections; one element of the State
Nation | People bound by common culture, history, language, sentiment | Psychological/cultural unity; may lack a State
Society | All social relationships of people | Wider than State; not territorial or coercive
Power vs authority (NCERT Sociology): authority = power accepted as legitimate, i.e. right and just; it rests on legitimacy
Modern States are defined by sovereignty, citizenship and often nationalism
Citizenship rights (T.H. Marshall line, NCERT): civil (speech, religion, property, equal justice), political (vote, stand for office), social (welfare, health, education)
⚠ "States" of the Indian Union or the 50 US States are not States in the political-science sense: they lack sovereignty
⚠ Stateless societies (anthropologists): order kept by kinship, cross-cutting alliances, rites, without government apparatus

t: Sovereignty → internal and external, attributes
text:
## 1. Meaning
From Latin Superanus = supreme; supreme and independent authority to legislate, govern and enforce without external interference
Internal sovereignty: supreme legal authority over all individuals and institutions inside the State
External sovereignty: freedom in foreign affairs from external control
## 2. Attributes (PMF list of six)
Attribute | Meaning
Absoluteness | Final, unquestionable authority within boundaries
Indivisibility | Cannot be shared among competing institutions
Permanence | Continues through changes of government
Originality | Arises from within, not conferred by others
Inalienability | Cannot be surrendered or permanently transferred
Universality | Applies to all persons, laws, institutions in the State
## 3. Historical roots
Event | Contribution
Peace of Westphalia (1648) | Exclusive State sovereignty; no external interference
Glorious Revolution (1688) | Sovereignty from monarch to accountable Parliament
French Revolution (1789) | Sovereignty belongs to the people
⚠ Brexit illustrates "no authority higher than the sovereign" (UK refused superiority of EU Parliament)

t: Sovereignty → kinds and where India places it
text:
## 1. Kinds
Kind | Who holds it
Legal | Body that makes law the courts enforce (UK: Parliament)
Political | Electorate / people whose will lies behind the law
Popular | The people as ultimate source (Rousseau; "We, the people")
De jure / de facto | Lawful claimant / one actually obeyed
## 2. Sovereignty in the Indian Constitution
Preamble: Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic; "We, the people" = popular sovereignty
India follows constitutional supremacy, not parliamentary sovereignty (UK)
Provision | Link to sovereignty
Art 1 | India a Union of States: indivisible territory
Art 2 | Parliament may admit or establish new States
Art 51 | Promote peace, keep external discretion
Art 51A(c) | Duty to uphold sovereignty, unity and integrity
Art 53 | Executive power of Union in the President
Third Schedule | Oaths affirm sovereignty and integrity
RPA s.29A(5) | Parties must affirm allegiance to sovereignty
## In news 2025-26
July 2025: Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar said India's sovereignty is non-negotiable; no external force can dictate internal or foreign policy (PMF Magnum)
Republic Day 2026: PMF LENS on "self-sovereignty": inner authority over one's actions without external coercion (ethics angle)

t: Sovereignty → limits and the Commonwealth trap
text:
## 1. Limits (PMF)
Limit | How it binds
Moral | Moral values, divine law, natural rights
Constitutional | Must work within the basic structure
International | Treaties, global legal norms, WTO rulings
Popular legitimacy | Depends on continuing public consent
Secession ban | No legal right of a unit to secede
## 2. Commonwealth
India stayed in the Commonwealth (1949) and accepts the British Crown as Head of the Commonwealth: an extra-constitutional declaration that does not curtail sovereignty
⚠ UPPCS 2017: "India is a member of the Commonwealth" correct; "sovereignty curtailed by it" wrong
Sovereign = neither a dependency nor a dominion of any nation

Austin (Analytical school): sovereign = determinate human superior who receives habitual obedience and obeys no one; Laski and pluralists attacked this monistic view (sovereignty shared with associations)

t: Constitutional government → limited government
text:
## 1. The most repeated answer of this topic (2014, 2020, 2021)
Constitutional government = limited government: powers defined and restricted by the Constitution; authorities act within constitutional limits, not arbitrarily
Year | Question | Correct answer | Wrong options
2021 | Constitutional government means | Government limited by the terms of the Constitution | Representative federal govt; head with nominal powers; head with real powers
2020 | Constitutional government by definition is | Limited government | Government by legislature; popular govt; multi-party govt
2014 | A constitutional government is one which | Restricts State authority in the interest of individual liberty | Restricts individual liberty in the interest of State authority
⚠ Direction of restriction is the trap: the Constitution limits the State for the individual, never the reverse
⚠ Nominal or real head, federal or unitary, one or many parties: these describe forms of government, not constitutionalism
PYQ 2014/2020/2021: same idea three times; expect it as a Statement-I/II next ("constitutional government limits power" + "because it rests on rule of law and separation of powers")

t: Constitution → its chief purpose and functions
text:
## 1. Chief purpose (2023)
To define and limit the powers of government
⚠ Distractors 2023: "determines objectives for making laws", "enables creation of political offices", "secures social justice": each is a function but not the chief one
## 2. Functions of a constitution (NCERT Class 11 line, beyond the PYQ)
Function | Meaning
Coordination and assurance | Basic rules that let members of a society trust each other
Specification of decision-making | Who has power to make decisions (allocation of power)
Limitations on government | Rights citizens hold that no government may violate
Aspirations and goals | Enables government to fulfil aspirations, create a just society
Fundamental identity | Gives people a collective political identity
Most common way to limit power: listing fundamental rights that no government may violate
PYQ 2023: "best reflects the chief purpose" → limiting function beats enabling function

t: Constitution vs constitutionalism
text:
## 1. PMF table
Constitution | Constitutionalism
Establishes governmental framework | Limits governmental power
Creates and distributes powers | Prevents arbitrary exercise of power
Can exist even under authoritarian rule | Requires genuinely limited government
Constitution organises power; constitutionalism limits it
⚠ Mere existence of a written constitution does not imply constitutionalism
## 2. Elements of constitutionalism (PMF, six)
Element | Content
Popular sovereignty | Ultimate authority with people via representatives
Rule of law | Government within legal limits
Separation of powers | Checks and balances
Independent judiciary | Guards Constitution and rights
Accountable government | Answerable for use of power
Civil authority | Military under civilian control
## In news 2025-26
May 2026: Supreme Court said majoritarianism cannot override constitutionalism in a constitutional democracy (PMF LENS, PTI)

t: Kinds of constitution → paired features

## 1. Pairs UPSC can test
Pair | Meaning | India
Written vs unwritten | Codified document vs conventions/statutes (UK) | Written, lengthiest
Rigid vs flexible | Hard vs easy to amend | Blend (simple, special, special + States' ratification)
Federal vs unitary | Constitutional division of powers vs central concentration | Federal with unitary bias; K.C. Wheare: "quasi-federal"
Procedural vs prescriptive | Only institutions/process vs also goals and values | Both elements
Independent judiciary is the essential feature showing federal character (PYQ 2021)
Granville Austin: cooperative federalism; Constitution "first and foremost a social document"
⚠ K.C. Wheare also said the Constitution balances rigidity and flexibility
## 2. UK vs India
UK | India
Parliamentary sovereignty | Constitutional supremacy
No judicial review of Acts | Judicial review (Arts 13, 32, 136, 137, 226, 227)
Rule of law is the higher principle (no written higher law) | Rule of law + written FRs + basic structure
PYQ 2021: Indian Parliament's power to legislate is limited, unlike the British; both statements correct

t: Constitutional morality → meaning and cases
text:
## 1. Meaning
Adherence to the values, principles and procedures of the Constitution even against popular/social morality
Ambedkar: constitutional morality "is not a natural sentiment; it has to be cultivated"

topic: Rule of Law and Due Process
t: Rule of law → Dicey's three features
text:
## 1. Origin
A.V. Dicey, British jurist, *Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution* (1885)
Borrowed from Britain (with parliamentary government, single citizenship, cabinet system, prerogative writs)
Dicey's element | Meaning | UPSC 2018 label
Supremacy of law / absence of arbitrary power | No one punished except for a distinct breach of law proved before ordinary courts | Limitation of powers
Equality before law | Equal subjection of all, officials included, to ordinary law by ordinary courts | Equality before law
Predominance of legal spirit | Constitution is the result, not the source, of individual rights defined by courts | Liberty and civil rights
⚠ "People's responsibility to the Government" is not a feature (2018 answer: 1, 2, 4 only)
⚠ Dicey opposed French droit administratif (special administrative courts for officials)
⚠ India keeps only the first two elements: here the Constitution is the source of rights, not the result
PYQ 2018: "how many/which" format with a plausible fake (citizen's duty); expect the same list in "How many of the above"

topic: Rule of Law and Due Process
t: Rule of law → in India and rule by law
text:
## 1. Indian anchor
Art 14: equality before law (British, negative) + equal protection of laws (American, positive); for all persons, citizens and foreigners
Rule of law is part of basic structure (Kesavananda 1973; Indira Nehru Gandhi 1975)
Arbitrariness is opposed to equality (Art 14): unguided, uncanalised discretion violates rule of law
Rule of law | Rule by law
Government under law | Government above law
Law must be just, fair, non-arbitrary | Law is only a tool of State control
Ruler also bound | Ruler exempt
⚠ PIL strengthens access to justice but is not a prerequisite of rule of law (existed before PIL through Arts 14, 32, 226)
NCERT: principal role of the judiciary is to protect rule of law and supremacy of law
## In news 2025-26
April 2025: Supreme Court on Prayagraj demolitions: demolishing homes without due process violates Art 21; "bulldozer justice" debate on rule of law

topic: Rule of Law and Due Process
t: Procedure established by law vs due process of law
text:
## 1. The 2023 question
Due process of law, in essence = the principle of natural justice (2023 answer)
Feature | Procedure established by law | Due process of law
Source | Japanese Constitution; text of Art 21 | US Constitution (5th and 14th Amendments)
Test | Law validly enacted and procedure followed | Law and procedure must also be just, fair, reasonable
Court's power | Narrow, literal; protects only against executive | Wide; protects against legislature too
Indian case | A.K. Gopalan (1950) | Maneka Gandhi (1978)
Maneka Gandhi: procedure must be fair, just and reasonable; linked Arts 14, 19, 21 = "golden triangle"; read substantive and procedural due process into Art 21
⚠ Options 2023: "procedure established by law" is the Indian text, not the meaning of due process; "fair application of law" and "equality before law" are partial
⚠ Words "due process" do not appear in the Indian Constitution
PYQ 2023: meaning-of-term question; next likely: "Maneka Gandhi introduced due process" as a statement (correct in substance)

topic: Rule of Law and Due Process
t: Natural justice → its two rules
text:
## 1. Principles
Maxim | Meaning
Nemo judex in causa sua | No one should be a judge in his own cause (rule against bias)
Audi alteram partem | Hear the other side; no one condemned unheard
Reasoned decision | Speaking order (added by courts)
Applied to administrative bodies: CAT is not bound by CPC but guided by natural justice; Speaker deciding anti-defection must give opportunity to respond
## 2. Article 21 expansions (all from "life and personal liberty")
Case | Right read into Art 21
Francis Coralie Mullin (1981) | Live with human dignity
Hussainara Khatoon (1979) | Speedy trial
Olga Tellis (1985) | Livelihood, shelter
M.C. Mehta (1987) | Pollution-free environment
D.K. Basu (1997) | Arrest/detention guidelines against custodial torture
Puttaswamy (2017) | Privacy

## In news 2025-26
2025-26: about 170 custodial deaths recorded; India has no anti-torture law, has not ratified UNCAT (CARE April 2026)
2026: highway safety ruling adds right to safe travel under Art 21 (CARE April 2026)
Oct-Nov 2026: PMF on due process in death penalty: Bachan Singh (1980) "rarest of rare"; Vasanta Sampat Dupare (2025): meaningful sentencing hearing is part of Arts 14 and 21

topic: Liberty, Law and Separation of Powers
t: Liberty → the definition UPSC accepts
text:
## 1. Answer 2019: opportunity to develop oneself fully
Option (2019) | Verdict
Protection against tyranny of political rulers | Negative, partial
Absence of restraint | Negative liberty only
Opportunity to do whatever one likes | Licence / anarchy
Opportunity to develop oneself fully | Positive liberty: correct
Liberty = absence of restraints plus opportunities for development of personality
Constitution's enabling measures (reservation, minority rights, Art 15 non-discrimination) create conditions to develop fully
⚠ Freedom is defined so each enjoys it without threatening the freedom of others or public order
PYQ 2019: positive-vs-negative liberty; 2018 and 2021 followed on the same theme (law, safeguards)

topic: Liberty, Law and Separation of Powers
t: Negative vs positive liberty
text:
## Beyond your notes
Negative liberty | Positive liberty
Freedom from interference | Freedom to realise one's potential
Area of non-interference by State | State creates enabling conditions
Classical liberals: Hobbes, Locke, J.S. Mill (harm principle) | T.H. Green, Rousseau, Laski
Minimal State | Welfare State
Distinction popularised by Isaiah Berlin, *Two Concepts of Liberty* (1958)
## 2. Mill (PMF)
Harm principle: free to act unless the action harms others (drunk-driving laws)
Free speech: truth emerges from open debate; also advocate of representative government and gender equality (*The Subjection of Women*)
## 3. Liberty in the Preamble
Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship (five; inspired by French Revolution)
⚠ Preamble does not say liberty of "action" or "vocation" (these were in the Objectives Resolution)

topic: Liberty, Law and Separation of Powers
t: Law and liberty → "no law, no liberty"
text:
## 1. Answer 2018
"If there is no law, there is no liberty" (John Locke): "where there is no law, there is no freedom"
Liberty is freedom from restraint and violence by others, which only law secures; not freedom to do as one pleases
Option (2018) | Why wrong
More laws, less liberty | Treats law only as restraint (negative view)
If liberty, laws must be made by the people | Confuses liberty with democracy
Laws changed often endanger liberty | Concerns stability, not the basic relationship
## 2. Locke's ideas (PMF)
Idea | Content
Natural rights | Life, liberty, property
State of nature | Generally peaceful, governed by natural law (Hobbes: "war of all against all")
Consent | Government legitimate by consent of the governed
Limited government, separation of powers | Restrain State power
Right to resistance | Against a government violating rights
Locke = "father of liberalism"
PYQ 2018: law as the condition of liberty, not its enemy

topic: Liberty, Law and Separation of Powers
t: Safeguard of liberty → separation of powers
text:
## 1. Answer 2021
Best safeguard of liberty in a liberal democracy = separation of powers
Option (2021) | Why not
Committed judiciary | Committed to the government's policy: never checks it
Centralisation of powers | Leads to authoritarianism
Elected government | Expected to secure liberty, but not the best safeguard
Separation of powers | Organs check each other; prevents arbitrary action
Liberal approach: power rooted in people's will; rule of law as foundation; separation of powers as vehicle of restraint
⚠ "Committed judiciary" was a 1970s phrase (supersession of judges, A.N. Ray 1973, M.H. Beg 1977)
## Beyond your notes
Montesquieu, *The Spirit of the Laws* (1748): liberty is lost if legislative, executive and judicial powers are united in one person or body
PYQ 2021: two-word trap: "committed judiciary" sounds good but is the opposite of an independent one

topic: Liberty, Law and Separation of Powers
t: Separation of powers → how India applies it
text:
## 1. Features
India: functional separation with checks and balances, not rigid (US model)
Executive drawn from and responsible to legislature (parliamentary), so legislature-executive fusion
Art 50 (DPSP): separate judiciary from executive in public services of the State
Separation of powers recognised as basic structure (after Kesavananda 1973; Indira Gandhi 1975)
Check | By whom
Judicial review of laws, executive acts | Judiciary
Removal of judges, impeachment of President | Legislature
No-confidence motion, questions | Legislature over executive
Appointment of judges, ordinances | Executive
## In news 2025-26
Oct 2026: CJI declined Opposition leaders' request for a meeting on allegations against the CEC during SIR, citing judicial independence and constitutional boundaries (PMF)
2025: 130th Constitution Amendment Bill (removal of PM/CM/Ministers after 30 days' detention) criticised for hitting presumption of innocence, separation of powers, collective responsibility (CARE Oct 2025)

t: Equality → absence of privileges
text:
## 1. Answer 2017
One implication of equality in society = absence of privileges
Formal equality first demanded to break feudal hierarchies of ranks and orders; privileges by gender, colour, creed, religion are irrational
Option (2017) | Verdict
Privileges | Correct: equality = no special privileges
Restraints | Equality coexists with restraints (laws)
Competition | Equal opportunity enables competition
Ideology | Unrelated
Testbook: equality = lack of special benefits for any group + equal chances for all
⚠ Equality before law (Art 14) = "absence of special privileges" in favour of any person (British, negative concept)
PYQ 2017: equality as negation of privilege; positive side = equal opportunity and reasonable classification

t: Equality → civic, political, economic in the Constitution
text:
## 1. Preamble: equality of status and of opportunity
Facet | Provisions
Civic | Art 14 (equality before law), 15 (no discrimination), 17 (untouchability abolished), 18 (titles abolished)
Political | Art 325 (no exclusion from rolls on religion, race, caste, sex), Art 326 (adult suffrage)
Economic | Art 39(a), (d) livelihood, equal pay for equal work; Art 16 equal opportunity in public employment
## 2. Equality before law vs equal protection
Equality before law | Equal protection of laws
British | American
Negative | Positive
Absence of special privileges | Like treated alike; equal treatment in equal circumstances
Equal subjection to ordinary law | Permits reasonable classification
Valid classification: intelligible differentia + rational nexus with the object
⚠ Formal (identical treatment) vs substantive equality (affirmative action to equalise outcomes)
Voting age 21 → 18 by 61st Amendment, 1988

t: Justice → social, economic, political
text:
## 1. Preamble justice (three kinds; Russian Revolution 1917)
Kind | Meaning
Social | Equal treatment without distinction of caste, colour, race, religion, sex; no privileges; uplift of SC, ST, OBC, women
Economic | No discrimination on economic grounds; remove glaring inequalities of wealth, income, property
Political | Equal political rights, equal access to offices, equal voice
Economic justice is in the Preamble and DPSPs (IAS 2013), e.g. Art 38(1)
⚠ Cultural or religious justice is not in the Preamble (UPPSC trap)
## 2. Theories
Thinker | Idea
Plato | Justice = each doing his own function; "minding one's own business"
Rawls (*A Theory of Justice*, 1971) | Justice as fairness; veil of ignorance; difference principle: inequalities only if they benefit the least advantaged
Amartya Sen | Justice must combine fairness with attention to actual human outcomes
## Beyond your notes
Distributive justice (Aristotle): fair distribution of goods and burdens; corrective justice rectifies wrongs

t: Fraternity → dignity, unity and integrity
text:
## 1. Content
Preamble: fraternity assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation
"Integrity" added by 42nd Amendment (1976) along with socialist, secular
Promoted by single citizenship and Art 51A(e) (spirit of common brotherhood)
Ideal | Inspiration
Liberty, equality, fraternity | French Revolution (1789)
Justice: social, economic, political | Russian Revolution (1917)
Idea of a Preamble | USA
Language of Preamble | Australia
Ambedkar: liberty, equality, fraternity form a union of trinity; to divorce one from the other defeats democracy
⚠ NCERT: Constitution reconciles liberal individualism with social justice and group (community) rights
## In news 2025-26
26 Nov 2025: Constitution Day (declared 2015, Ambedkar's 125th birth-anniversary year) highlighted justice, liberty, equality, fraternity, rule of law

t: Rights → claims of citizens against the State
text:
## 1. Answer 2017
Rights are claims of the citizens against the State: entitlements that bind the State to respect life, liberty, equality
Option (2017) | Verdict
Claims of the State against citizens | Reversed: those are duties/obligations
Privileges incorporated in a Constitution | Rights are not privileges; not only constitutional
Claims of citizens against the State | Correct
Privileges of a few against the many | Opposite of equality
Laski: rights are "those conditions of social life without which no man can seek to be himself at his best"
⚠ Rights are not privileges: equality means absence of privileges (2017 twin question)
PYQ 2017: three rights-and-duties questions in one paper; the theory angle peaked 2017

t: Rights ↔ duties → correlative
text:
## 1. Answer 2017
In India, rights are correlative with duties: two faces of the same thing
Holland: every right implies active or passive forbearance by others; that forbearance is a duty
Ernest Barker: "Rights without duties are like men without shadows"
Option (2017) | Verdict
Rights correlative with duties | Correct
Rights personal, independent of society | Rights exist only in society
Rights, not duties, advance personality | One-sided
Duties, not rights, stabilise the State | One-sided
⚠ Same year trap: Fundamental Duties are not correlative to legal duties and have no legislative process for enforcement (2017 answer: neither)
## 2. Fundamental Duties facts
Part IVA, Art 51A; 42nd Amendment 1976 on Swaran Singh Committee; idea from USSR
Originally 10, now 11 (51A(k), 86th Amendment 2002: parent to provide education 6-14)
Non-justiciable

t: Rights → kinds UPSC can name
text:
## 1. Classification
Kind | Meaning | Example
Natural | Inherent, prior to the State (Locke) | Life, liberty, property
Moral | Backed by conscience, not enforceable | Respect from children
Legal | Recognised and enforced by the State | FRs, statutory rights
Civil | Personal freedom | Speech, religion, property, equal justice
Political | Participation | Vote, contest, hold office
Social/economic | Welfare | Education, health, work
Indian FRs: originally seven, now six (Right to Property removed by 44th Amendment 1978, now Art 300A)
FRs evolved from negative restraints on the State to positive guarantees of dignity (Art 21)
## Beyond your notes
Negative rights (State must refrain: speech, Art 19) vs positive rights (State must provide: Art 21A education)
Human rights: UDHR, 10 Dec 1948; India's Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
⚠ Indian Constitution: FRs justiciable (Part III), DPSPs non-justiciable (Part IV, Art 37)

t: Democracy → its superior virtue
text:
## 1. Answer 2017
Democracy's superior virtue: it calls into activity the intelligence and character of ordinary men and women
Option (2017) | Why wrong
Methods of strengthening executive leadership | That is efficiency, not democracy's virtue
A superior individual with dynamism and vision | Leader-centric (elitism, dictatorship)
A band of dedicated party workers | Party-centric
Participation develops citizens' responsibility and political awareness (Mill: participation improves collective intelligence)
Lincoln: government of the people, by the people, for the people
⚠ Not democratic: "supreme power vested solely in one person, like a king"
PYQ 2017: virtue lies in ordinary people, not leaders or parties

t: Democracy → direct vs representative, and forms of government
text:
## 1. Types
Type | Feature | Example
Direct | People decide themselves | Gram Sabha, Swiss cantons; referendum, initiative, recall
Representative | Decisions by elected representatives | Parliament, State legislatures
NCERT: direct democracy impossible for crores of people, so rule by people = rule by representatives
Local self-government = democratic decentralisation (PYQ 2017), not direct democracy
## 2. Forms of government
Form | Feature
Autocracy | Supreme power in one individual/entity
Monarchy | Hereditary ruler
Dictatorship | Absolute power, no effective limits
Republic | Elected head of State; India's President indirectly elected
Parliamentary | Executive responsible to legislature (UK)
Presidential | Separate fixed-term executive (USA)
Democracy in Preamble = political, social and economic democracy
## In news 2025-26
Jan 2025 (in PMF Magnum 2026): 75 years of the Republic: reflection on universal adult franchise and democratic journey (PMF Magnum)

t: Gandhism vs Marxism → stateless society
text:
## 1. Answer 2020: common agreement = final goal of a stateless society
Point | Gandhism | Marxism
Final goal | Stateless society (enlightened anarchy, village swaraj) | Stateless, classless communist society
View of State | Violence in concentrated form | Tool of class oppression; will wither away
Means | Non-violence, truth, satyagraha | Class struggle, revolution, dictatorship of proletariat
Property | Trusteeship | Abolition of private property; common ownership
History | Moral and spiritual | Economic determinism (historical materialism)
⚠ Class struggle, abolition of private property, economic determinism: Marxist only, Gandhi rejected all three
Sociology: functionalist view: State represents all; conflict view: State represents dominant sections
PYQ 2020: one shared end, different means

t: Ideologies → liberalism, socialism, secularism
text:
## 1. Key ideas
Ideology | Core
Liberalism | Individual liberty, limited government, rights; Locke "father"
Socialism | Reduce inequality; public ownership/planning
Indian socialism | Democratic socialism, mixed economy (Nehru rejected Soviet total State ownership)
Anarchism | Abolish the State
"Socialist", "secular" added by 42nd Amendment; Minerva Mills (1980) affirmed socialism as guiding principle
## 2. Secularism: Western vs Indian (NCERT)
Western | Indian
Mutual exclusion: State and religion strictly separate | Principled distance: State may intervene or abstain
Neither help nor hinder religion | Equal respect; can reform (e.g., temple entry)
Secularism in basic structure: S.R. Bommai (1994)
## In news 2025-26
Nov 2024 (PMF, July 2025 recap): Supreme Court dismissed petitions against "socialist" and "secular" in the Preamble; these terms do not impede legislation or FRs

t: Political protests → origin of the terms
text:
## 1. Answer 1996: Boycott comes from the name of a person
Captain Charles Cunningham Boycott, land agent in Ireland, ostracised by tenants in the Irish Land War, 1880
Term | Origin / meaning
Boycott | Person's name (Ireland, 1880)
Gherao | Hindi "encircle": surrounding officials until demands met; not part of Art 19(1)(b) peaceful assembly

topic: Demand for a Constituent Assembly and its composition
t: Demand for a Constituent Assembly → who, when
text:
Year | Step
1934 | Idea first put forward by M.N. Roy
1934 | First formal demand: Swaraj Party (Ranchi, May 1934) (ROCKET)
1935 | INC officially demanded a Constituent Assembly
1938 | Nehru: a Constitution framed by a CA elected on adult franchise, without outside interference
1940 | August Offer: British accepted the demand in principle
1942 | Cripps Proposals: constitution-making after World War II; Muslim League rejected it
1946 | Cabinet Mission Plan gave the actual scheme for the CA
Cabinet Mission: Pethick-Lawrence (Chairman), Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander; arrived 24 March 1946; plan announced 16 May 1946 with Viceroy Wavell
Cabinet Mission had a short-term aim (interim government) and a long-term aim (Constitution by a CA)
⚠ The idea is M.N. Roy's (1934); the first official INC demand is 1935; the scheme came from the Cabinet Mission (1946), not Cripps
PYQ 2015: Cabinet Mission recommended a federal government; it did not enlarge Indian courts' powers or add Indians to the ICS

topic: Demand for a Constituent Assembly and its composition
t: Cabinet Mission seat plan → numbers
text:
Unit | Seats (1946) | After Partition
Governors' Provinces (11) | 292 | Provinces: 229
Chief Commissioners' Provinces (4) | 4 | (in 229)
Princely States | 93 | 70
Total | 389 | 299
Seats roughly in proportion to population: 1 seat per 10 lakh (1 million) people
Provincial seats divided among three communities: General, Muslim, Sikh (Sikh only in Punjab), in proportion to population
Section A (Hindu-majority provinces): 187 seats (167 General + 20 Muslim)
3 June 1947 plan (Partition): members from areas going to Pakistan ceased to be members
⚠ British India total = 296 (292 + 4), not 292; total 389, reduced to 299
⚠ Ratio was 1:10 lakh, not 8, 11 or 12 lakh (UPPCS 2001 options)

topic: Demand for a Constituent Assembly and its composition
t: Election of members → how they were chosen
text:
Group | Method
Provincial members | Indirectly elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies (set up under the GoI Act 1935)
Voting system | Members of each community in the Assembly elected their own: proportional representation by single transferable vote (STV)
Princely States | Nominated by the rulers (method by consultation)
Provincial Legislative Assemblies were themselves elected in January 1946 on a restricted franchise (tax, property, education)
So the CA was partly elected, partly nominated and not based on universal adult franchise
Why not adult franchise? The Mission feared it would delay the Constitution
PYQ option (2002, 2013) | Right?
Directly elected by the people | No
Nominated by INC and Muslim League / by the parties | No
Nominated by the British Parliament or Governor-General | No
Selected by the Government for expertise | No
Elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies | Yes
⚠ "Directly elected by the people" is the trap: election was indirect
PYQ 2002 and 2013: both asked how members were chosen; answer: elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies
PYQ 2004: "CA was elected by the Provincial Assemblies in 1946" is correct; Jinnah was not a member

Not a representative body: not elected by adult franchise | Members of all communities represented; elections indirect
Not sovereign: created by British proposals | Became fully sovereign under the Indian Independence Act 1947

Every State and local authority shall endeavour to provide facilities for mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups
