PYQ 2023: of four statements only the Puducherry > Arunachal one was correct ("only one")

t: Election process → STV, quota, nomination
text:
## 1. How it is run
Proportional representation by single transferable vote, secret ballot
Quota = (total value of valid votes ÷ 2) + 1: more than half needed
Lowest candidate eliminated; ballots transferred by next preference until quota reached
Item | President | Vice-President
Proposers + seconders | 50 + 50 | 20 + 20
Security deposit | ₹15,000 | ₹15,000
Deposit forfeited below | 1/6 of votes polled | 1/6
Conducted by | ECI | ECI
Law | Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 | same Act
⚠ Rajya Sabha polls use open ballot; Presidential poll uses secret ballot
⚠ "Proportional representation" here gives one winner: it is really a majority system with preferences

t: Election disputes (Art 71) → acts done remain valid
text:
## 1. Article 71
Rule | Content
Who decides | Supreme Court only; decision final
Vacancy in electoral college | Not a ground to challenge the election
Election declared void | Acts done before the SC decision remain valid
Other matters | Parliament may regulate by law
Assemblies dissolved and elections pending: the Presidential election cannot be postponed
Constitution prescribes no time limit for assent to a Bill (Art 111) = pocket veto
⚠ All three 2023 statements were false: acts not invalid, election not postponed, no assent time limit
PYQ 2023: answer "None"; each statement reversed a rule above

t: Qualifications, oath, conditions → what Art 58-60 require
text:
## 1. Qualifications (Art 58)
Citizen of India; completed 35 years; qualified for election to Lok Sabha; no office of profit
Not offices of profit: President, VP, Governor, Union or State Minister
## 2. Oath (Art 60)
Point | President | VP (Art 69)
Administered by | CJI (else senior-most SC judge) | President or person appointed
Content | Preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law; serve people | Bear true faith and allegiance; faithfully discharge duty
Person acting as President takes a similar oath
⚠ Lok Sabha qualification for President, Rajya Sabha for VP; both need 35 years (not 25 or 30)
## In news 2025-26
Next Presidential election due before the term of Droupadi Murmu (in office since 25 July 2022) ends in July 2027
## Beyond your notes
Murmu (15th President) took office 25 July 2022 (as of 2026; verify)

t: Term, resignation and vacancy → who, when, how long
text:
## 1. Article 56, 57, 62
Event | Rule
Term | 5 years from entering office; continues till successor enters
Resignation | Addressed to the Vice-President (VP informs LS Speaker)
Re-election | Eligible, no limit on terms (Art 57)
Vacancy by expiry | Election completed before expiry
Casual vacancy (death, resignation, removal) | Election within 6 months (Art 62)
Person elected to casual vacancy | Gets a full 5-year term
Same "full term" rule for the VP; but VP casual vacancy has no 6-month deadline
⚠ Resignation goes to the VP, not to the CJI, PM or Speaker

t: Who acts as President → succession chain
text:
## 1. Art 65 and beyond
Situation | Who discharges functions
Vacancy (death, resignation, removal) | Vice-President acts till new President enters (max 6 months)
Absence, illness, inability | Vice-President discharges functions
Both President and VP offices vacant | CJI; else senior-most available SC judge
Acting person gets all powers, immunities, emoluments of the President
VP while acting ceases to function as RS Chairman; no Chairman's salary
Indian VP only acts; does not succeed for the remaining term (unlike the US)
⚠ The Speaker is not in the line of succession
## Beyond your notes
Presidential (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969: provides for CJI acting; CJI M. Hidayatullah acted in 1969

t: Impeachment (Art 61) → procedure step by step
text:
## 1. Ground and steps
Only ground: "violation of the Constitution" (undefined)
Step | Requirement
Initiation | Either House
Notice | 14 days' written notice to the President
Signatures | 1/4 of total members of the initiating House
Passing | 2/3 of total membership of initiating House
Investigation | Other House investigates; President may appear / be represented
Sustaining | 2/3 of total membership of other House: removed from that date
Quasi-judicial procedure; no President impeached so far
⚠ Majority is of total membership, not "present and voting"
⚠ Nominated MPs take part; State Assemblies do not
PYQ 1996: State Legislative Assemblies elect but do not impeach; Councils do neither

t: Election vs impeachment → who participates
text:
## 1. The swap UPSC tests
Body | Elects President | Impeaches President | Elects VP | Removes VP
Elected MPs | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes
Nominated MPs | No | Yes | Yes | Yes
Elected MLAs | Yes | No | No | No
MLCs | No | No | No | No
State Legislatures: role only in electing the President
Nominated MPs: out only of the Presidential election
⚠ Option "State Legislative Councils" is wrong for both election and impeachment

t: Immunities (Art 361) → what the President is shielded from
text:
## 1. During term
Matter | Protection
Official acts | Not answerable to any court
Criminal proceedings | None can be started or continued
Arrest / imprisonment | No process
Civil proceedings (personal acts) | Allowed after two months' notice
Official-act immunity does not bar investigation of an impeachment charge
Governors enjoy the same protections under Art 361
⚠ Personal immunity does not shield the office from judicial review of prolonged inaction (SC, 2025 Reference)

topic: Legislative Powers: Assent, Veto and Ordinance
t: Legislative powers → complete list
text:
## 1. What the President does in Parliament
Power | Detail
Summon / prorogue | Both Houses; dissolve Lok Sabha
Joint sitting | Summons (presided by Speaker)
Address | First session after each general election and first session of each year
Nomination | 12 to RS (literature, science, art, social service)
Anglo-Indians | 2 to LS, ended by 104th Amdt, 2019
Disqualification of MPs | Decides, on ECI's opinion (Art 103)
Prior recommendation | Money Bills, new State / boundary Bills
Assent | Art 111
Ordinance | Art 123
Presiding | Appoints a member to preside if Speaker + Deputy (or Chairman + Deputy) both vacant
⚠ Anti-defection disqualification is decided by the Speaker/Chairman, not the President

topic: Legislative Powers: Assent, Veto and Ordinance
t: Article 111 → President's options on a Bill
text:
## 1. Options by type of Bill
Bill | Assent | Withhold | Return
Ordinary Bill | Yes | Yes | Yes, once
Money Bill | Yes | Yes | No
Constitution Amendment Bill | Must assent | No | No
Re-passed after return (with or without amendments): must assent
Assent to Amendment Bills made obligatory by the 24th Amdt, 1971
Constitution sets no time limit for the President's decision
⚠ Money Bill: assent or withhold only; it cannot be returned (it is introduced on the President's own recommendation)

topic: Legislative Powers: Assent, Veto and Ordinance
t: Veto types → which the Indian President has
text:
## 1. Four vetoes compared
Veto | Meaning | India?
Absolute | Withholds assent; Bill dies | Yes
Suspensive | Returns non-Money Bill; overridden by ordinary majority | Yes
Pocket | Takes no action indefinitely | Yes
Qualified | Overridden only by higher majority | No (USA has it)
Absolute veto used: Rajendra Prasad, PEPSU Appropriation Bill (1954); R. Venkataraman, MPs' Salary Bill (1991)
Pocket veto: Zail Singh, Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986
US President must act in 10 days: Indian President's "pocket is bigger"
⚠ Governor has absolute and suspensive veto but no pocket veto (Testbook)
⚠ Pocket veto not available on Constitution Amendment Bills

topic: Legislative Powers: Assent, Veto and Ordinance
t: Reserved State Bills (Art 201) → President's options
text:
## 1. Art 200 to Art 201
Step | Rule
Governor (Art 200) | Assent / withhold / return non-Money Bill / reserve for President
Mandatory reservation | Bill endangering High Court's position
President (Art 201) | Assent / withhold / direct Governor to return (non-Money Bill)
State re-passes within 6 months | President not bound to assent
Parliament can override the suspensive veto on Central Bills; a State Legislature cannot override on reserved Bills
## In news 2025-26
8 Apr 2025 (Tamil Nadu v Governor): 2-judge bench set 3-month deadline for President under Art 201, used Art 142 for "deemed assent" to 10 TN Bills
President then made an Art 143 Reference; Nov 2025, 5-judge Constitution Bench opined:
Opinion | Point
Fixed timelines | Courts cannot impose on Governor or President
Deemed assent | Rejected
Merits of decision | Not justiciable before Bill becomes law
Prolonged inaction | Limited mandamus possible
Art 143 on every reserved Bill | Not required
⚠ CARE summary: April 2025 ruling; PMF: opinion delivered Nov 2025; the Reference does not overrule, it clarifies

topic: Legislative Powers: Assent, Veto and Ordinance
t: Ordinance (Art 123) → conditions and duration
text:
## 1. When and how long
Point | Rule
When | Both Houses not in session, or either House not in session
Need | Satisfied circumstances require immediate action
Satisfaction | Subject to judicial review
Laid | Before both Houses on reassembly
Lapse | 6 weeks after reassembly (later date if Houses reassemble on different dates)
Earlier end | Disapproval resolutions by both Houses / withdrawal by President
Advice | Promulgation and withdrawal on CoM advice
Maximum life ≈ 6 months + 6 weeks (gap between sessions ≤ 6 months)
D.C. Wadhwa (1987): repeated re-promulgation unconstitutional
Governor's parallel: Art 213 (needs President's instructions in three cases)
⚠ Cannot be issued when both Houses are sitting; can be issued when only one is in session
PYQ 2003: assent to the 2002 electoral reforms ordinance returned unchanged by Cabinet was under Art 123

topic: Legislative Powers: Assent, Veto and Ordinance
t: Ordinance scope → what it can and cannot do
text:
## 1. Co-extensive with Parliament's power
Can | Cannot
Amend or repeal any Central Act or another ordinance | Amend the Constitution
Operate retrospectively | Abridge Fundamental Rights (it is "law" under Art 13)
Modify tax laws | Go beyond Union / Concurrent subjects (except in Emergency: State List too)
Same force as an Act; temporary
⚠ "Can abridge FRs" is the trap: ordinance is law under Art 13(3)
PYQ 2025: statements 1 (amend Central Act) and 3 (back date) correct; 2 (abridge FR) wrong
## In news 2025-26
Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026: SC strength 34 → 38 (37 + CJI); revived debate on ordinance misuse (LENS Jun 2026)
Replaced by a Bill introduced in Lok Sabha (LENS Jul 2026); PMF Polity book records the Amendment Act, 2026 (33 → 37 other judges)
Income-tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026: replaced by Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
## Beyond your notes
Krishna Kumar Singh (2017): re-promulgation is a fraud on the Constitution; failure to lay an ordinance before the legislature is a serious breach
38th Amdt (1975) made satisfaction non-justiciable; 44th Amdt (1978) removed that bar

t: Reports laid before Parliament → which the President must lay
text:
## 1. "Causes to be laid before each House"
Report / document | Article
Finance Commission recommendations + explanatory memorandum | 281
CAG reports on Union accounts | 151
UPSC annual report | 323
NCSC reports | 338
Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities reports | 350B
Annual Financial Statement (Budget) | 112
Art 354 order modifying revenue distribution (Emergency) | 354
PAC report is Parliament's own committee report: not laid by the President
State side: CAG State reports, SPSC, SFC go to the Governor
⚠ Finance Commission recommendations are laid by the President, not the Finance Minister, PM or Speaker
PYQ 2012: FC, CAG, NCSC laid by President; PAC report was the odd one out
PYQ 2010: Art 281 duty belongs to the President
## Beyond your notes
NCST (Art 338A) and NCBC (Art 338B) reports are also laid by the President

t: Executive powers → whom the President appoints
text:
## 1. Appointments and other executive functions
Category | Who
Ministers | PM and other Ministers (on PM's advice)
Law officer | Attorney General (holds during pleasure)
Constitutional bodies | CAG, CEC and ECs, UPSC Chairman and members, Finance Commission
States / UTs | Governors; Administrators of UTs
Commissions | Backward classes commission (Art 340), Inter-State Council (Art 263)
Other | Declares Scheduled Areas
Seeks information from PM on administration and legislative proposals (Art 78)
Makes regulations for A&N Islands, Lakshadweep, DNH and DD (Puducherry only when Assembly suspended/dissolved)
⚠ State PSC members and State Election Commissioner are appointed by the Governor

t: Financial, military, diplomatic, emergency → remaining powers
text:
## 1. One line each
Power | Content
Money Bill | Only on President's recommendation (Art 110/117)
Demands for grants | Only on President's recommendation
Contingency Fund of India | Advances for unforeseen expenditure
Finance Commission | Constitutes every 5 years (Art 280)
Military | Supreme Commander; declares war / peace subject to Parliament
Diplomatic | Treaties in his name; sends and receives ambassadors
Emergency | 352 (national), 356 (State), 360 (financial)
Judicial | Appoints CJI and SC/HC judges; Art 143 reference; Art 72 pardon
⚠ War and peace are declared by the President but regulated by Parliament (Art 53(2))

t: Art 143 advisory jurisdiction → President's reference to SC
text:
## 1. Two clauses
Clause | Matter | Court
143(1) | Question of law or fact of public importance | May refuse to answer
143(2) | Pre-Constitution treaties, sanads (excluded from Art 131) | Must answer
Heard by a bench of at least 5 judges (Art 145(3)); no response deadline
Opinion not binding under Art 141; cannot overturn settled judgments
Invoked around 15 times; reference made on CoM advice
⚠ The President is not bound by the SC's advisory opinion

t: Pardoning power (Art 72) → five forms
text:
## 1. Forms of clemency
Form | Meaning
Pardon | Removes both sentence and conviction
Commutation | Substitutes a lighter form of punishment
Remission | Reduces period without changing character
Respite | Lesser sentence due to special circumstances (e.g., pregnancy)
Reprieve | Temporary stay of execution, esp. death sentence
## 2. Three cases where Art 72 applies
Offence against a Union law
Sentence by a Court Martial
Death sentence (any law)
⚠ Remission keeps the nature of punishment; commutation changes it

t: President vs Governor pardon → Art 72 vs Art 161
text:
## 1. Comparison
Point | President (Art 72) | Governor (Art 161)
Laws covered | Union law | State law
Court Martial | Yes | No
Death sentence: pardon | Yes | No
Death sentence: suspend, remit, commute | Yes | Yes
Acts on | Union CoM advice | State CoM advice
Even if a State law prescribes death, the power to pardon lies only with the President
⚠ Governor cannot pardon a death sentence but can commute it
## In news 2025-26
PMF 2026: Governor may ask the State Cabinet to reconsider a mercy / remission recommendation if facts were missed
In Re: Policy Strategy for Grant of Bail (SC): States/UTs must frame a remission policy within 2 months; consider eligible convicts without application; reasoned orders (remission under Art 72 / 161 and statutory powers)

t: Pardon and judicial review → what the courts held
text:
## 1. Cases
Case | Holding
Maru Ram (1980) | Art 72 power subject to judicial review; exercised on CoM advice
Kehar Singh (1988) | President may examine evidence afresh; no oral hearing; not a court of appeal
Shatrughan Chauhan (2014) | Inordinate delay and mental illness = grounds for commutation
President need not give reasons; a second mercy petition after rejection cannot get a stay
⚠ The power is not discretionary: exercised on Union Cabinet advice
⚠ Review is limited: courts do not judge the merits
PYQ 2025: "limited judicial review" true; "without advice of Central Government" false
## Beyond your notes
Epuru Sudhakar (2006): clemency order quashed; review on grounds of mala fides, irrelevant or extraneous considerations, non-application of mind, arbitrariness, discrimination

t: Vice-President Articles 63-71 → what each says
text:
## 1. Article map
Article | Provision
63 | There shall be a Vice-President
64 | Ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (also Art 89)
65 | Acts as President / discharges functions
66 | Election, qualifications
67 | Term 5 years; (a) resignation to President; (b) removal; (c) continues till successor
68 | Time of election to fill vacancy
69 | Oath before President
70 | Discharge of President's functions in other contingencies
71 | Election disputes: Supreme Court
Second-highest office; first in line of succession; modelled on the US VP
⚠ VP resigns to the President; President resigns to the VP

t: President vs Vice-President election → the differences
text:
## 1. Side by side
Point | President | Vice-President
Electoral college | Elected MPs + elected MLAs (States, Delhi, Puducherry) | All MPs: elected and nominated
State legislatures | Participate | Do not
Vote value | Varies (MLA formula; MP 700) | Equal for every MP
Qualification | Qualified for LS | Qualified for RS
Proposers + seconders | 50 + 50 | 20 + 20
Method | PR-STV, secret ballot | PR-STV, secret ballot
Original Constitution: VP elected at a joint meeting of both Houses; changed by 11th Amdt, 1961
⚠ Nominated MPs: out of Presidential election, in VP election
PYQ 2013: statement 2 (nominated MPs vote only for VP) correct

t: Chairman of Rajya Sabha → member or not
text:
## 1. Chairman vs Deputy Chairman
Point | Chairman (VP) | Deputy Chairman
Member of RS? | No (ex-officio) | Yes, elected from among members
Vote | Casting vote only, in a tie | Votes as member
Removal | Only by removal as VP | RS resolution, majority of all then members (Art 90)
Salary | As Chairman of RS (no salary as VP) | As Deputy Chairman
Chairman decides anti-defection cases for RS members; decisions subject to judicial review
Money Bill certification is the Speaker's, not the Chairman's
⚠ Chairman is not a member; Deputy Chairman is
PYQ 2013: "Chairman and Deputy Chairman are not members" was false
## In news 2025-26
Harivansh re-elected Deputy Chairman (3rd time, April 2026), by voice vote under Rule 7; first nominated member to become Deputy Chairman

t: Removal of the Vice-President → resolution, not impeachment
text:
## 1. Art 67(b)
Step | Rule
Ground | None specified
Initiated | Only in Rajya Sabha
Notice | 14 days', stating intent and reasons
RS majority | Majority of all the then members (effective majority)
Lok Sabha | Agrees (simple majority)
Not "impeachment": no charge, no investigation, no 2/3
⚠ Cannot start in LS, either House, or a joint sitting
## 2. President vs VP removal
Point | President | VP
Method | Impeachment | Resolution
Ground | Violation of Constitution | None
Initiated in | Either House | RS only
Majority | 2/3 total membership, both Houses | Effective majority RS + LS agrees
PYQ 2004: resolution can be moved in Rajya Sabha alone

t: Qualifications and term → Art 66-67
text:
## 1. Requirements
Citizen; 35 years; qualified for election to Rajya Sabha; no office of profit
Must be a registered elector (in any parliamentary constituency)
Cannot be a member of any legislature: seat vacated on entering office
Point | Rule
Term | 5 years from entering office
Re-election | Eligible, no limit
Expiry vacancy | Election before expiry
Casual vacancy | Election "as soon as possible": no 6-month limit
New VP | Full 5-year term
Acting VP | None provided; Deputy Chairman presides over RS
⚠ The 6-month rule is for the President only (Art 62)

t: Vice-President in news 2025-26 → resignation and election
text:
## In news 2025-26
Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned mid-term (July 2025), resignation effective on submission, no acceptance needed
Event | Detail
Mid-term vacancies (PMF) | V.V. Giri resignation 1969, Krishan Kant death 2002, Dhankhar 2025
Interim | Deputy Chairman Harivansh presided over RS
Election (Sept 2025) | C.P. Radhakrishnan (NDA) defeated B. Sudershan Reddy (joint opposition)
Turnout | Over 98% of MPs voted; 13 abstained
Returning Officer | P.C. Mody, RS Secretary General
⚠ CARE (July 2025) lists V.V. Giri and R. Venkataraman as earlier mid-term resignations; PMF counts vacancies (Giri, Krishan Kant)
Dr S. Radhakrishnan: first VP (1952-62), then second President (1962-67)
## Beyond your notes
Dhankhar resigned on 21 July 2025 citing health; election held 9 Sept 2025: Radhakrishnan 452, Reddy 300 votes (verify)

topic: Prime Minister: appointment, membership and tenure
t: Appointment of the PM → who appoints and when discretion arises
text:
## 1. Constitutional rule
Point | Fact
Article | Art 75(1): PM appointed by the President
Procedure for selection | Not prescribed in the Constitution; governed by convention
Normal case | Leader of the majority party/coalition in Lok Sabha
Proof of majority before appointment | Not required (Delhi HC, 1980); floor test within a reasonable period
Election of PM beyond judicial review | Tried by 39th Amdt 1975 (Art 329A); repealed by 44th Amdt
## 2. Situational discretion of the President
Hung Lok Sabha: appoint person most likely to command confidence; ask for a vote of confidence (Testbook: "within a month")
Sudden death of PM with no obvious successor; once the party elects a leader, President must appoint him
First use: 1979, N. Sanjiva Reddy appointed Charan Singh after Morarji Desai's fall
1998: K.R. Narayanan asked Vajpayee for letters of support and a confidence vote within 10 days
⚠ President has no constitutional discretion here, only situational discretion (PMF)

topic: Prime Minister: appointment, membership and tenure
t: Membership of Parliament → which House and the six-month rule
text:
## 1. Rules
Question | Answer
Must the PM be an MP when appointed? | No (SC, 1997)
Deadline to become an MP | Six months (consecutive), else ceases to be PM
Which House? | Either House: Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha
Must it be Lok Sabha? | No (unlike UK, where PM comes from the Commons by convention)
Re-appointment without election after six months | Not allowed (S.R. Chauhan v State of Punjab, 2001)
## 2. PMs from Rajya Sabha (Testbook)
Indira Gandhi (1966), H.D. Deve Gowda (1996), Manmohan Singh (2004)
⚠ "Must become a member of the Lok Sabha within six months" is the classic wrong option: it is either House
PYQ 2012: PM at appointment need not be an MP but must become a member of one of the Houses within six months

topic: Prime Minister: appointment, membership and tenure
t: PM from Rajya Sabha → speak vs vote in Lok Sabha
text:
## 1. Article 88
Right in the other House | Minister / PM | Attorney General
Speak and take part in proceedings | Yes | Yes
Take part in a joint sitting and committees where named | Yes | Yes
Vote in a House he is not a member of | No | No (no vote anywhere)
So a Rajya Sabha PM can speak on the Budget, make statements in Lok Sabha, reply to debates
He cannot vote on a no-confidence motion (decided only by Lok Sabha)
⚠ A Rajya Sabha PM need not shift to Lok Sabha within six months
⚠ State parallel: Art 177 for state ministers
PYQ 1997: a Rajya Sabha PM "will not be able to vote in his favour in a no-confidence motion" was the only correct option

topic: Prime Minister: appointment, membership and tenure
t: Oath, term and removal → what the text says
text:
## 1. Rules
Item | Fact
Oath of office and oath of secrecy | Administered by the President (Third Schedule)
Tenure | Not fixed; holds office during the pleasure of the President
Real condition | Continues while he has the confidence of the Lok Sabha
Limit on number of terms | None
Salary | Fixed by Parliament; MP's salary plus allowances
Death / resignation of PM | Whole Council of Ministers dissolves
Death / resignation of a minister | Only a vacancy
## 2. Caretaker government
Not in the Constitution; a resigned/defeated ministry asked to continue till a new one takes over
Confines itself to routine administration; avoids major policy decisions
Example: V.P. Singh resigned (1990) after losing support in Lok Sabha
⚠ Oath of secrecy is taken by PM and ministers, not by the President

topic: Prime Minister: appointment, membership and tenure
t: Written provision vs convention → which is which
text:
## 1. Classification UPSC tests
Practice | Status
PM appointed by President; ministers on PM's advice | Written (Art 75(1))
CoM collectively responsible to Lok Sabha | Written (Art 75(3))
15% cap | Written (Art 75(1A), 91st Amdt)
Leader of majority party becomes PM | Convention
PM resigns on losing majority in Lok Sabha | Convention
Ranks of ministers (Cabinet, MoS, Deputy) | Convention / practice
Deputy PM, Kitchen Cabinet, Cabinet Committees | Extra-constitutional
Leader of the House; LoP needs 10% seats | Rules / convention
Finance Minister must be from Lok Sabha | Neither (no such rule)
## Beyond your notes
If both President and Vice-President offices are vacant, the Chief Justice of India (or senior-most SC judge) acts as President under the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969, not the Speaker
PYQ 1995: asked which is not in the Constitution but followed as convention; answer: PM resigns on losing Lok Sabha majority; trap: "Speaker acts as President"

topic: Powers and functions of the Prime Minister
t: Executive power of the Union → President or PM
text:
## 1. Formal vs real
Provision | Content
Art 53 | Executive power vested in the President, exercised directly or through subordinate officers
Art 74(1) | CoM headed by PM to aid and advise the President
Art 77(1) | All executive action expressed in the name of the President
President | Nominal / de jure executive, Head of State
PM | Real / de facto executive, Head of Government
## 2. Case law
Shamsher Singh (1974): "satisfaction of the President" means satisfaction of the Council of Ministers
U.N.R. Rao (1971): CoM does not cease when Lok Sabha is dissolved; President must always have ministerial advice
⚠ Executive power is vested in the President, NOT the PM; executive action is in the President's name, NOT the PM's (UPSC 2014 too)
PYQ 2015: both statements wrong: executive power with PM; PM chairs Civil Services Board

topic: Powers and functions of the Prime Minister
t: PM and the Council of Ministers → powers
text:
## 1. Powers over ministers
Power | Detail
Choice of ministers | Full discretion: President appoints on PM's advice (Art 75(1))
Non-MPs as ministers | Allowed for six months
Portfolios | Allocates and reshuffles (formally by President on PM's advice)
Removal | Asks a minister to resign or advises President to dismiss
Meetings | Presides over Cabinet and CoM
Ranks | Allots ranks: Cabinet, MoS, Deputy
PM is the "keystone of the Cabinet arch", primus inter pares (Lord Morley); Laski: central to its "formation, life and death"
Nehru: PM is the "linchpin of Government"; Ambedkar: the PM, not the President, compares with the US President
## 2. Limits in coalition era (NCERT)
Since 1989: more presidential discretion, consultation with allies, curbs on choosing ministers and portfolios; PM as "negotiator"
⚠ PM is NOT limited to choosing MPs only, and does NOT need the President's counselling
PYQ 1996: PM "has full discretion in the choice of persons to serve as ministers"

topic: Powers and functions of the Prime Minister
t: Article 78 → PM's duties towards the President
text:
## 1. Three duties
Clause | Duty
78(a) | Communicate all decisions of the CoM on Union administration and proposals for legislation
78(b) | Furnish information on administration and legislative proposals as the President calls for
78(c) | If President requires, submit for CoM consideration a matter decided by a single minister but not considered by the Council
## 2. Appointments on PM's advice
Attorney General, CAG, Election Commissioners, UPSC members, Finance Commission members, Governors
State parallel: Art 167 (Chief Minister's duties to the Governor)
⚠ Art 78 is the PM's duty; the President's right to be informed flows from it; it is not Art 74
PYQ 2013: "PM shall communicate to the President about proposals for legislation" was correct

topic: Powers and functions of the Prime Minister
t: PM and Parliament, other roles → what he heads
text:
## 1. Parliament
Leader of the House in Lok Sabha (if a member; else a minister he nominates); Rajya Sabha leader is a minister nominated by PM
Advises President on summoning, prorogation and dissolution of Lok Sabha
Announces major policies; steers the legislative agenda
## 2. Bodies chaired by the PM
Body | PM's role
NITI Aayog | Chairperson
Nuclear Command Authority, Political Council | Head
Cabinet Committee on Security and most cabinet committees | Chair
Appointments Committee of the Cabinet | Chair
Selection panels (CBI Director, CVC, CIC, NHRC, Lokpal, CEC/ECs) | Chair, with LoP
## In news 2025-26
18th Lok Sabha has a LoP after a ten-year gap (no party had 10% seats earlier)
2023 CEC/EC Act: panel of PM, LoP and a Cabinet Minister nominated by PM; SC split verdict on referring the challenge to a Constitution Bench (LENS Sept 2026)

topic: Powers and functions of the Prime Minister
t: Cabinet Secretariat and PMO → who heads what
text:
## 1. Offices
Office | Fact
Cabinet Secretariat | Directly under the PM; NOT under the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Cabinet Secretary | Administrative head; senior-most civil servant; ex-officio Chairman, Civil Services Board
Appointment of Cabinet Secretary | By ACC, chaired by PM
Precedence | Cabinet Secretary 11th (with AG and LGs in their UTs)
Business Rules | Cabinet Secretariat administers Allocation and Transaction of Business Rules, 1961 (Art 77(3))
PMO | Began as PM's Secretariat (1947), renamed PMO in 1977; headed administratively by the Principal Secretary
⚠ Civil Services Board is chaired by the Cabinet Secretary, NOT the PM
## In news 2025-26
Seva Teerth (Dec 2025): name of the new Central Vista complex (earlier "Executive Enclave") for PMO, Cabinet Secretariat, NSCS and India House
Kartavya Bhavan (Aug 2025): first building of the Common Central Secretariat on Kartavya Path
Oct 2026: Cabinet Secretariat declined to act on two ECs' complaint against an IAS officer at ECI, citing the constitutional body's autonomy

topic: Council of Ministers: Articles 74-78 and collective responsibility
t: Article 74 → nature of ministerial advice
text:
## 1. Evolution
Stage | Position
Original 74(1) | CoM to aid and advise; binding nature not explicit
42nd Amdt 1976 | Advice made binding ("shall act in accordance")
44th Amdt 1978 | President may return advice once for reconsideration; reconsidered advice binding
Art 74(2) | Advice tendered cannot be inquired into by any court
Courts can still review the constitutional validity of the action taken (PMF)
K.R. Narayanan returned advice on President's Rule in UP (1997) and Bihar (1998)
⚠ Reconsideration is allowed only once; there is no second return
⚠ State parallel Art 163(3): advice to Governor not inquired into; but Governor has constitutional discretion (163(1)-(2)), the President has none

topic: Council of Ministers: Articles 74-78 and collective responsibility
t: Article 75 → what each clause says
text:
## 1. Clauses
Clause | Content
75(1) | PM appointed by President; other ministers on PM's advice
75(1A) | Total ministers including PM ≤ 15% of Lok Sabha strength (91st)
75(1B) | Member disqualified for defection cannot be a minister till term ends or re-election (91st)
75(2) | Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President
75(3) | CoM collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha
75(4) | President administers oaths of office and secrecy
75(5) | Non-member for six consecutive months ceases to be minister
75(6) | Salaries and allowances fixed by Parliament
⚠ Ministers serve at the pleasure of the President, NOT the PM (formally)
⚠ Testbook quotes the tribal-welfare proviso under "75(6)": that proviso is Art 164(1) (States)
## 2. Other articles of the set
Art 77: action in President's name; authentication; rules of business (77(3))
Art 88: ministers speak in both Houses; vote only in own House
Art 352(3): only place the word "Cabinet" appears (44th Amdt)

topic: Council of Ministers: Articles 74-78 and collective responsibility
t: Article 77 and Business Rules → who creates ministries
text:
## 1. Authority
Act | Done by
Rules for transaction of business and allocation among ministers | President (Art 77(3))
Creation of ministries/departments | President on PM's advice under Allocation of Business Rules, 1961
Assignment of a ministry to a minister | President on PM's advice
Cabinet Committees | Provided for under Transaction of Business Rules, 1961
## 2. Numbers and history
Ministries on 15 Aug 1947: 18; at present 53 (Preview)
Portfolio system: begun by Lord Canning, Indian Councils Act 1861
⚠ Ministries are NOT created by the PM on the Cabinet Secretary's advice
## In news 2025-26
Aug 2026: Ministry of Culture's "Festival of India" mandate cited as flowing from the Allocation of Business Rules
PYQ 2009: statement 1 (PM creates ministries on Cabinet Secretary's advice) wrong; statement 2 (President assigns ministries on PM's advice) right

topic: Council of Ministers: Articles 74-78 and collective responsibility
t: Collective responsibility → to whom and what it means
text:
## 1. Meaning
Point | Fact
Responsible to | Lok Sabha only (Art 75(3)); NOT Rajya Sabha, NOT "Parliament", NOT President
No-confidence passed | Entire CoM resigns, including Rajya Sabha ministers
No-confidence against one minister | Whole ministry falls (NCERT)
Cabinet decisions | Bind all ministers; dissenter must resign
Alternative on defeat | Advise dissolution (President not bound to accept)
No-confidence motion | Moved by Opposition in Lok Sabha (Rule 198)
Confidence motion | Moved by the government
Ministers may come from either House, yet answer only to Lok Sabha
⚠ Rajya Sabha cannot pass a no-confidence motion against the government
PYQ 2007: A (responsible to both Houses) false, R (members of both Houses can be ministers) true
PYQ 2013: "collectively responsible to the Parliament" was the wrong statement

topic: Council of Ministers: Articles 74-78 and collective responsibility
t: Individual and legal responsibility → how they differ
text:
## 1. Three kinds
Kind | Basis | Practice
Collective | Art 75(3) | "Swim or sink together"
Individual | Art 75(2) (pleasure) | President removes a minister on PM's advice, even if CoM has LS confidence
Legal | None in India | No countersignature of President's orders by ministers (UK has it)
Ministers answer to Parliament for lapses of their bureaucrats (ministerial responsibility)
Authenticated orders cannot be questioned on the ground that the President did not personally make them (Art 77(2))
⚠ India has no legal responsibility of ministers; courts cannot inquire into advice

topic: Council of Ministers: Articles 74-78 and collective responsibility
t: Union and State provisions → matching Articles
text:
## 1. Parallel Articles
Subject | Union | State
CoM to aid and advise | 74 | 163
Appointment, cap, responsibility | 75 | 164
Action in Head's name; business rules | 77 | 166
Duties of PM / CM | 78 | 167
Ministers' rights in Houses | 88 | 177
## 2. State-only features
Minimum 12 ministers (164(1A)); responsible to the Legislative Assembly only
Tribal welfare minister compulsory in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP, Odisha (164(1)); 94th Amdt 2006 removed Bihar
Governor has constitutional discretion; President does not
## In news 2025-26
Sept 2026: Telangana CM had a minister removed; Governor acts on CM's advice under Art 164 (Praveen CA 360)

topic: 91st Amendment and size of the ministry
t: 91st Amendment 2003 → every change it made
text:
## 1. Changes
Provision | Change
Art 75(1A) | Union CoM incl. PM ≤ 15% of Lok Sabha
Art 75(1B) | Defector barred from being a Union minister
Art 164(1A) | State CoM incl. CM ≤ 15% of Assembly, not less than 12
Art 164(1B) | Defector barred from being a State minister
Art 361B | Defector barred from any remunerative political post
Tenth Schedule | Split (one-third) exception deleted; only merger (two-thirds) protected
Cap counts the PM/CM himself
⚠ The 15% is of the Lower House (Lok Sabha / Assembly), NOT of both Houses or of the ruling party
⚠ P-MCA mentions a minimum of 7 for Sikkim, Mizoram, Goa and Arunachal; PMF and Testbook give the constitutional floor as 12
PYQ 2009 and 2007: identify the amendment (91st) among 90th, 92nd, 93rd, 95th, 97th

topic: 91st Amendment and size of the ministry
t: Why the cap → background and reform ideas
text:
## 1. Reasons (NCERT)
Before 2003 size was set by "exigencies"; led to jumbo ministries
In hung Houses, posts were used to win over MPs/MLAs (defection inducement)
## 2. 2nd ARC proposal (Testbook)
Assembly strength | Suggested cap
Above 200 | 10%
80-200 | 12%
Below 80 | 15%
2nd ARC: effective devolution under 73rd/74th Amdts would shrink state ministries
## Beyond your notes
With 543 Lok Sabha seats, the Union ceiling works out to 81 ministers including the PM
Neighbouring numbers: 92nd (Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali to 8th Schedule), 93rd (OBC reservation in private institutions), 97th (cooperatives) (verify)

topic: 91st Amendment and size of the ministry
t: Disqualified persons as ministers → rules and cases
text:
## 1. Bars and cases
Rule / case | Holding
Art 75(1B)/164(1B) | Defector cannot be a minister till term ends or re-elected
S.R. Chauhan (2001) | Non-member cannot be re-appointed after six months without election
B.R. Kapoor (2001) | Cited by Testbook on appointment of non-legislators
Manoj Narula (2014) | No constitutional bar on persons with criminal background as ministers; left to PM's discretion
## Beyond your notes
B.R. Kapoor (2001): a person convicted and disqualified from contesting cannot be appointed CM even for six months
## In news 2025-26
Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2025 (Aug 2025, referred to a JPC): amends Arts 75, 164, 239AA
Minister (incl. PM/CM) arrested and detained 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with 5+ years: removed on PM's/CM's advice, or ceases automatically on the 31st day
Re-appointment allowed after release; parallel changes for UTs (1963 Act) and J&K (2019 Act); backdrop: V. Senthil Balaji case (2023)

topic: Ranks of ministers, Cabinet and cabinet committees
t: Ranks of ministers → constitutional or convention
text:
## 1. Categories
Rank | Role | In Cabinet?
Cabinet Minister | Heads key ministries (Home, Finance, Defence, External Affairs) | Yes
MoS (Independent Charge) | Runs a ministry without a Cabinet minister above | No (attends when invited)
Minister of State | Attached to Cabinet minister, specific functions | No
Deputy Minister | Assists Cabinet minister / MoS | No
Parliamentary Secretary | Assists in parliamentary work | Not in CoM
Constitution does not classify ministers into ranks: British practice and parliamentary convention
Sec 2, Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952 gives the classification legislative sanction (PYQ key)
⚠ "Constitution classifies ministers into four ranks" is FALSE
PYQ 2022: statement 1 (four constitutional ranks) false, statement 2 (15% incl. PM) true

topic: Ranks of ministers, Cabinet and cabinet committees
t: Council of Ministers vs Cabinet → differences
text:
## 1. Comparison
Council of Ministers | Cabinet
Larger body (about 60-80) | Smaller core (about 15-20)
All categories of ministers | PM + Cabinet ministers only
Constitutional: Arts 74, 75 | Word added only to Art 352(3) by 44th Amdt 1978
Rarely meets as a whole | Meets regularly; collective decisions
Implements Cabinet decisions | Directs CoM; decisions bind all ministers
Collectively responsible to Lok Sabha | Enforces collective responsibility
For Art 352, "Cabinet" = PM + ministers of Cabinet rank appointed under Art 75; its written advice is needed for a National Emergency
⚠ The original Constitution did not use the word "Cabinet"

topic: Ranks of ministers, Cabinet and cabinet committees
t: Cabinet committees → chair and function
text:
## 1. Major committees (PMF)
Committee | Function | Chair
Political Affairs (CCPA) | Domestic and foreign policy; "Super-Cabinet" | PM
Economic Affairs (CCEA) | Economic coordination (e.g. MSP, FRP) | PM
Appointments (ACC) | Top appointments (Cabinet Secretary etc.) | PM
Security (CCS) | Defence, national security, nuclear doctrine | PM
Investment and Growth | Investment policy | PM
Employment and Skill Development | Jobs, skills | PM
Parliamentary Affairs | Govt business in Parliament | Not PM
Accommodation (CCA) | Govt accommodation | Home Minister
## 2. Nature
Extra-constitutional; set up by the PM under the Transaction of Business Rules, 1961; standing or ad hoc
When the PM is a member, he presides; Cabinet can review their decisions
CCS permanent members: PM, Defence, Home, Finance, External Affairs; NSA, Cabinet Secretary, service chiefs attend as invitees
⚠ Parliamentary Affairs committee: PMF says chaired by the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs; Preview says by the Defence Minister
## In news 2025-26
CCS (Apr 2025) decisions included suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty; CCEA fixed sugarcane FRP (2026-27) and raw jute MSP (Rs 5,925/qtl, 2026-27)

topic: Ranks of ministers, Cabinet and cabinet committees
t: Deputy PM, Kitchen Cabinet, GoMs → status
text:
## 1. Extra-constitutional offices and bodies
Item | Status
Deputy Prime Minister | Not in the Constitution; political post; only a Cabinet minister in law
First Deputy PM | Sardar Patel (1947-50)
Kitchen / Inner Cabinet | Informal; PM + trusted advisers, may include non-ministers
Groups of Ministers (GoMs) | Ad hoc, inter-ministerial; some empowered to decide
Cabinet Committees | Extra-constitutional, under Business Rules
2nd ARC: use GoMs selectively, with clear mandate and time limits
## Beyond your notes
Other Deputy PMs: Morarji Desai, Charan Singh, Jagjivan Ram, Y.B. Chavan, Devi Lal, L.K. Advani
K.M. Sharma v Devi Lal (1990): oath as "Deputy PM" valid since he is just a minister; title confers no extra power
⚠ Kitchen Cabinet can include persons outside the CoM; Cabinet committees comprise ministers
## In news 2025-26
2025 marked Sardar Patel's 150th birth anniversary (first Deputy PM and Home Minister)

topic: Composition and duration of the Houses
t: Parliament → what it consists of (Art 79)
text:
## 1. Three parts
Part | Fact
President | Not a member of either House, but an integral part of Parliament
Rajya Sabha | Council of States, Upper House, "House of Elders", red carpet
Lok Sabha | House of the People, Lower House, green carpet
Articles 79-122, Part V; Westminster model
President's parliamentary roles: assent, summon, prorogue, dissolve LS, address
⚠ "Parliament consists of LS and RS only" is false (2012): the President is part of it
⚠ US President is not part of Congress; Indian President is part of Parliament
PYQ 2012: all three statements false (UTs are in RS; CEC does not decide election disputes; President is part of Parliament)

topic: Composition and duration of the Houses
t: Rajya Sabha → strength, election, nominated members (Art 80)
text:
## 1. Composition
Item | Fact
Maximum | 250 = 238 States and UTs + 12 nominated
Present | 245 (233 elected + 12 nominated)
Seat allocation | Fourth Schedule; by population (unequal, unlike US Senate)
State members | Elected by elected MLAs by PR-STV; open ballot (RPA amended 2003; upheld in Kuldip Nayar 2006)
UTs with RS seats | Delhi, Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir only
Nominated | Literature, science, art, social service (Art 80(3)); idea from Ireland
Nominated members: can join a party within 6 months; vote in VP election but not President's; none made a minister so far
Polls held only if candidates exceed vacancies
⚠ Sports is not one of the four nomination fields
⚠ UTs are represented in RS (only three of them)
## In news 2025-26
Apr 2026: Harivansh re-elected Deputy Chairman a third time, by voice vote; first time a nominated member holds the post

topic: Composition and duration of the Houses
t: Lok Sabha → strength, seats and reservation (Art 81, 330)
text:
## 1. Composition
Item | Fact
Maximum | 550 = up to 530 States + 20 UTs
Present | 543 elected (18th LS: 524 States + 19 UTs)
Anglo-Indian nomination | 2 seats (Art 331) ended by 104th CAA, 2019
SC / ST seats | 84 SC, 47 ST of 543
SC/ST reservation | Extended to 25 Jan 2030 (104th CAA)
Electorate | No separate electorates; all voters vote in reserved seats
System | Direct, FPTP, territorial constituencies
Art 81(2): states under 6 million population exempt from equal population-seat ratio
⚠ Praveen Sir CA (Apr 2026) writes LS maximum 552; that was before the 104th CAA; PMF gives 550
⚠ ROCKET Sheets writes "530 States + 13 UTs"; PMF/LENS give 524 + 19

topic: Composition and duration of the Houses
t: Lok Sabha seats → amendments that changed them
text:
## 1. Amendment map
Amendment | Change
7th (1956) | Raised elected seats from States (reorganisation)
31st (1973) | Raised elected strength 525 → 545 (new NE states, 1971 census)
42nd (1976) | Froze inter-state seat allocation at 1971 census till 2000
84th (2001) | Freeze extended till first census after 2026; constituencies readjusted
87th (2003) | Delimitation on 2001 census (not 1991)
104th (2019) | Ended Anglo-Indian nomination
106th (2023) | One-third seats for women (Art 330A)
Art 82: readjustment after every census; Delimitation Commissions 1952, 1963, 1973, 2002
⚠ 2003 traps: 6th-22nd, 13th-38th, 11th-42nd; answer 7th and 31st
⚠ The 2026 date does not mean automatic delimitation in 2026
## Beyond your notes
7th CAA set the cap at 500 elected (verify)
PYQ 2003: amendments raising members from States = 7th and 31st

topic: Composition and duration of the Houses
t: Duration of Houses → term, retirement, extension (Art 83)
text:
## 1. Terms
House | Term
Rajya Sabha | Permanent, never dissolved; 1/3 retire every 2nd year; member term 6 years fixed by RPA 1951 (not Constitution)
Lok Sabha | 5 years from first meeting; dissolves automatically at end; may be dissolved earlier by President
LS in National Emergency | Extended by law one year at a time, any number of times; not beyond 6 months after Emergency ends
State Assembly | Same rule as LS
Casual vacancy in RS filled for the remainder of the term
⚠ Term is extended "one year at a time", not six months or two years (2002)
⚠ RS can be prorogued but not dissolved
PYQ 2002: LS term can be extended by one year at a time during Emergency

topic: Composition and duration of the Houses
t: Lok Sabha expansion → 131st Amendment Bill 2026
text:
## 1. The Bill
Item | Detail
Seats | LS 543 → 850 (815 States, 35 UTs); max 550 → 850
Articles | 81, 82, 334A
Aim | Early delimitation on 2011 census; enable women's quota before 2029
Companion | Delimitation Bill, 2026: commission chaired by an SC judge
Fate | Defeated in LS: 298 for, 230 against of 528; needed 326 (special majority, Art 368)
Concerns: southern states' weight, RS weight in joint sittings, 15% ministry cap (81 → ~133)
LS sittings fell from ~135 days/year (1st LS) to ~55 (17th LS)
⚠ LENS-CA (Aug 2026) mentions an 816/824-seat pro-rata formula; PMF LENS (Apr 2026) gives 850

topic: Membership: qualifications, disqualification, office of profit
t: Qualifications → Art 84 and RPA
text:
## 1. Who can be an MP
Requirement | Lok Sabha | Rajya Sabha
Citizen of India | Yes | Yes
Minimum age | 25 | 30
Oath (Art 84 + Third Schedule) | Yes | Yes
Registered elector | In any parliamentary constituency (RPA 1951) | Same
Reserved seat | Must be SC/ST | -
Age ladder: MP-LS 25, MP-RS 30, President/VP/Governor 35; Panchayat/municipality 21
⚠ RS age is 30, not 35 (35 is for President, VP, Governor)

topic: Membership: qualifications, disqualification, office of profit
t: Disqualification → grounds and who decides (Art 102, 103)
text:
## 1. Grounds
Source | Grounds
Art 102 | Office of profit (unless exempted by Parliament); unsound mind (court); undischarged insolvent; not a citizen / foreign allegiance; any law of Parliament
RPA 1951 | Electoral offences, corrupt practices, convictions, failure to lodge expenses, govt contracts, dismissal for corruption
Tenth Schedule | Defection
## 2. Deciding authority
Ground | Decided by
Art 102 grounds | President, bound by Election Commission's opinion (Art 103)
Defection | Speaker / Chairman, subject to judicial review (Kihoto Hollohan 1992)
Election disputes | High Court under RPA (appeal to SC)
⚠ The CEC does not adjudicate election disputes (2012 trap)
⚠ For Art 102, the President must follow the EC's opinion

topic: Membership: qualifications, disqualification, office of profit
t: Office of profit → Act of 1959
text:
## 1. Facts
Point | Fact
Definition | Not defined in the Constitution; built by court rulings
Meaning | Post bringing gain or benefit; amount immaterial
Purpose | Separation of powers between legislature and executive
Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 | Lists exempted posts (e.g. ministers, Leader of Opposition)
Amended | 5 times: 1993, 1999, 2000, 2006, 2013
Example | Jaya Bachchan (RS) disqualified for UP Film Development Council chair
Joint Committee on Offices of Profit examines which posts should disqualify
Same bar applies to President, VP, Governor (Art 58, 66, 158)
⚠ "Office of profit is well-defined in the Constitution" is false
PYQ 2019: statements 1 and 2 correct (Act exempts posts; amended five times)

topic: Membership: qualifications, disqualification, office of profit
t: Vacation of seats → Art 101 situations
text:
## 1. When a seat falls vacant
Case | Rule
Double membership | Both Houses: choose within 10 days or RS seat vacates; MP + MLA: state seat vacates if not resigned (in time)
Resignation | LS member to Speaker; RS member to Chairman; may be refused if not voluntary
Absence | 60 days without permission: House may declare vacant (Art 101(4))
Others | Election void, expulsion, elected President/VP, appointed Governor
60 days exclude prorogation and adjournments over 4 consecutive days; leave granted max 59 days at a time; Committee on Absence of Members
No MP has lost a seat under Art 101(4)
⚠ Vacancy for absence is not automatic: the House must declare it
## In news 2025-26
MP Amritpal Singh (NSA detention) feared losing his seat under Art 101(4)

topic: Membership: qualifications, disqualification, office of profit
t: Oath, penalty and salaries → Art 99, 104, 106
text:
## 1. Facts
Article | Rule
99 | Oath before President or person appointed by him
Before oath | Cannot vote or take part; no privileges
104 | Sitting/voting without oath or when disqualified: ₹500 per day
106 | Salaries fixed by Parliament by law; pension by law, not by Constitution
Oath form in the Third Schedule; members swear allegiance to the Constitution and to uphold sovereignty and integrity
⚠ Pension for MPs is statutory, not constitutional

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Speaker → election and tenure (Art 93, 94)
text:
## 1. Election
Point | Fact
Elected by | Lok Sabha from among its members (must be a member when elected)
Date of election | Fixed by the President
Majority | Simple majority of members present and voting
Qualification | None beyond membership
## 2. Vacates office if
Ceases to be an LS member
Resigns in writing to the Deputy Speaker
Removed by resolution of majority of all the then members (effective majority) after 14 days' notice
## 3. Continuity
On dissolution, Speaker stays till immediately before the first meeting of the new LS
⚠ Speaker does not hold office at the President's pleasure (2012 trap)
⚠ No "become a member within 6 months" rule for the Speaker (that is for ministers)
PYQ 2012: only "resigns to Deputy Speaker" correct; PYQ 2025 and 2004: Speaker survives dissolution

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Speaker removal → procedure and rights (Art 94, 96)
text:
## 1. Procedure (LS Rules 200-203)
Step | Rule
Notice | Written, to Secretary-General; 14 days before moving
Leave | At least 50 members must stand in support
Discussion | Within 10 days of leave; confined to the charges
Passing | Majority of all the then members (effective majority)
## 2. Speaker during the motion (Art 96)
Right | Yes / No
Preside | No
Speak and take part | Yes
Vote in first instance | Yes
Casting vote | No
Deputy Speaker's removal: same; he cannot preside but may be present
⚠ The Speaker can speak and can vote on his own removal (2024 trap)
PYQ 2024: answer "1 only" (shall not preside); PYQ 2025: removal by majority of all then members, 14 days' notice
## In news 2025-26
Feb-Mar 2026: Opposition moved a removal notice against Speaker Om Birla in the Budget Session

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Speaker removal motions → history
text:
## 1. Earlier motions (all defeated)
Year | Speaker
1954 (CARE) / 1951 (P-MCA) | G.V. Mavalankar
1966 | Hukam Singh
1987 | Balram Jakhar
No Speaker has ever been removed
Removed Speaker remains an MP
⚠ PMF P-MCA dates the Mavalankar motion 1951; CARE (Feb 2026) gives 1954
⚠ Nabam Rebia (2016): Speaker cannot decide disqualification pleas while a removal notice against him is pending

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Speaker → powers and functions
text:
## 1. Powers
Power | Source / fact
Order, interpretation of rules | Final authority in the House
Quorum | Adjourns/suspends if no quorum (Art 100)
Casting vote | Only in a tie; no vote in first instance (Art 100)
Money Bill | Decides; decision final (Art 110)
Joint sitting | Presides (Art 108/118)
Tenth Schedule | Decides disqualification; judicial review; within 3 months (Keisham Meghachandra 2020)
Committees | Appoints chairpersons; chairs Business Advisory, Rules, General Purposes Committees
Ex officio | President of Indian Parliamentary Group; chairs Conference of Presiding Officers
Expunction | LS Rules 380-381 (RS Chairman: Rule 261)
Derives power from Constitution, Rules of Procedure, conventions
⚠ The Chairman of RS does not certify Money Bills or preside over joint sittings

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Speaker → independence and party membership
text:
## 1. Safeguards
Safeguard | Detail
Security of tenure | Removal only by effective majority
Salary | Fixed by Parliament, charged on Consolidated Fund (Art 97)
Conduct | Discussed only on a substantive motion
Proceedings | Not questioned in court for procedural irregularity (Art 122)
Precedence | 7th in order of precedence
Party: Constitution does not require resigning from party; Tenth Schedule permits leaving party without disqualification; no Speaker has done so
Convention: Speaker from the ruling party
⚠ Resigning from party on election is a British convention, not an Indian rule (2025 trap)
PYQ 2025: answer "1 and 3 only"

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Deputy Speaker → election, powers, conventions (Art 93-95)
text:
## 1. Facts
Point | Fact
Election | After Speaker; date fixed by the Speaker
Resigns to | Speaker
Removal | Effective majority, 14 days' notice
Status | Not subordinate to Speaker; responsible to House
Presiding | Same powers as Speaker; no appeal against rulings
Joint sitting | Presides if Speaker absent
Committees | Becomes chairman of any committee he is a member of
Oath | No separate oath
Office from opposition = convention only; Constitution sets no time limit to elect one
Notice of motion for his election is given by any member to the Secretary-General
⚠ No mandatory rule that he be from the opposition or ruling party (2022)
⚠ "Motion moved by Speaker, seconded by PM" is not the practice (2022)
PYQ 2022: answer "1 and 3 only"
## In news 2025-26
Deputy Speaker posts vacant in 8 state assemblies (Art 178); Jharkhand without one for 21 years

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Pro tem Speaker and panels → who presides when
text:
## 1. Who presides
Situation | Presides
Speaker absent | Deputy Speaker
Both absent | Member of Panel of Chairpersons (nominated by Speaker)
Both posts vacant | Member appointed by President (not a panel member)
First sitting of new LS | Pro tem Speaker
## 2. Pro tem Speaker
Appointed by President; usually senior-most member; President administers his oath
Administers oath to new members; conducts election of Speaker; office ends then
State assembly: appointed by Governor
⚠ A panel member cannot preside when both posts are vacant

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Chairman and Deputy Chairman of RS → how they differ (Art 64, 89-92)
text:
## 1. Chairman
Point | Fact
Who | Vice-President, ex officio (Art 64); not a member of RS
Removal | Only by removal as VP: RS effective majority + LS agreement, 14 days' notice; no grounds stated
Vote | Casting vote only
During VP removal resolution | Cannot preside; may speak; cannot vote at all
Money Bill / joint sitting | No role
## 2. Deputy Chairman
Elected by RS from its members (Art 89); resigns to Chairman; removal by effective majority of RS
Presides when VP resigns, without becoming VP; Panel of Vice-Chairpersons (nominated by Chairman)
⚠ Speaker on his removal can vote in first instance; Chairman on VP removal cannot vote
## In news 2025-26
Jul 2025: VP Jagdeep Dhankhar resigned (third mid-term vacancy after V.V. Giri 1969, Krishan Kant's death 2002); C.P. Radhakrishnan now Chairman
Apr 2026: Vice-Chairpersons panel reconstituted (6 members)

topic: Presiding officers: Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman
t: Speakers and firsts → person and record
text:
## 1. Records

t: Classes of bills → the four types and who can introduce

t: Ordinary Bill → stages in each House
text:
Stage | What happens
First reading | Leave to introduce; title and objectives read; published in the Gazette (may be published before introduction)
Second reading | Most important: general discussion, possible reference to a Select / Joint Committee or circulation for public opinion, then clause-by-clause consideration and amendments
Third reading | Debate only on accepting or rejecting the bill as a whole; no amendments
Second House | Pass as received, pass with amendments, reject, or take no action
Assent | President: assent, withhold, or return once for reconsideration (Art 111)
No fixed time limit for the second House on an ordinary bill; deadlock → joint sitting (Art 108) after 6 months
If returned bill is passed again, with or without amendment, President must assent
⚠ General discussion is at the second reading, not the first or third (Rocket sheet trap)
Absolute veto used: Rajendra Prasad, PEPSU Appropriation Bill, 1954; pocket veto: Zail Singh, Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill, 1986

t: Private Member's Bill → meaning and record
text:
Bill moved by any MP who is not a Minister: elected or nominated, in either House
Drafted by the member; introduced on Fridays (Private Members' Business); same stages as Government Bills
Government Bill | Private Member's Bill
Introduced by a Minister | By a non-Minister MP
Reflects government policy | Reflects member's stand
Drafted by department with Law Department | Drafted by member
Higher chance of passage | Lower chance
Defeat has political implications | Defeat does not imply loss of confidence
Only 14 PMBs enacted since Independence; last in 1970
⚠ 2017 statements both false: a private member is not only a nominated member; a PMB was not passed "for the first time" recently

t: Money Bill (Art 110) → what it must contain only
text:
A bill is a Money Bill if it contains only provisions on one or more of:
Clause | Matter
110(1)(a) | Imposition, abolition, remission, alteration, regulation of any tax
(b) | Borrowing or guarantees by the Government of India
(c) | Custody of the CFI or Contingency Fund; payment into / withdrawal from them
(d) | Appropriation of money out of the CFI
(e) | Declaring expenditure charged on the CFI, or increasing it
(f) | Receipt of money on account of CFI or Public Account; audit of Union / State accounts
(g) | Matters incidental to the above
Not a Money Bill merely because it provides for:
Fines or pecuniary penalties
Fees for licences or services
Tax by a local authority for local purposes
⚠ Appropriation out of the Contingency Fund is not in Art 110: only custody of it is (2018 answer)

Step | Rule

Certificate | Speaker decides and endorses the certificate; decision final (Art 110(3))
Rajya Sabha | Cannot reject or amend; may only recommend; must return within 14 days
Lok Sabha | May accept or reject any or all recommendations
RS silent 14 days | Deemed passed by both Houses in LS form
Joint sitting | None
President | Assent or withhold; cannot return for reconsideration
Cannot be referred to a Joint Committee (PMF infographic)

Introduced | LS only | LS only | Either House

Rajya Sabha | Only recommends | Can amend or reject | Can amend or reject
Joint sitting | No | Yes | Yes
